deduped_items.body_text:
•Dr Tunji Alausa, Minister of Education
…Plans digital tracking of lecturers, equipment, facilities
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja
ABUJA — The Federal Government has moved to overhaul the accreditation system for Nigerian universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, warning institutions against presenting a false or temporary picture of their academic and infrastructural capacity during accreditation exercises.
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, gave the warning in Abuja on Tuesday while inaugurating a Ministerial Committee on Strengthening the Accreditation and Quality Assurance System for Tertiary Institutions in Nigeria.
Alausa said the era of temporarily assembling lecturers, equipment and facilities ahead of accreditation visits must end, stressing that institutions should be assessed on resources that are genuinely available and sustainable.
He said the government would deploy digital technology, identity-management systems, geospatial mapping and other verification mechanisms to ensure that what institutions present to accreditation teams reflects their actual capacity.
“An institution should not be able to prepare a temporary picture of itself simply for the purpose of an accreditation visit. Sadly, this is what we see in a majority of instances,” the minister said.
Alausa expressed concern over the temporary movement of academic and non-academic personnel between institutions, as well as the borrowing or relocation of laboratory equipment, workshop resources, library materials and other facilities solely to impress accreditation teams.
He said such practices undermined the integrity of the tertiary education system and denied students access to the resources and personnel used to secure approval for academic programmes.
“We must ensure that when an accreditation team visits an institution, what it sees and verifies should represent the actual and sustainable capacity of that institution, not an arrangement assembled for the accreditation exercise,” he said.
Digital tracking of facilities, equipment
To close the loopholes, Alausa directed the National Universities Commission, NUC; National Board for Technical Education, NBTE; and National Commission for Colleges of Education, NCCE, to progressively move away from predominantly manual and episodic accreditation procedures to a digital, data-driven and continuously verifiable system.
He said geospatial mapping, geotagging and digital identification technologies should be considered for physical infrastructure, laboratories, workshops and major equipment presented during accreditation.
Under the proposed system, critical equipment used to secure accreditation would have unique digital records linked to the institution and its physical location, making it difficult for institutions to borrow or move resources merely to pass accreditation.
The minister said the same principle should apply to lecturers and other personnel.
He called for a comprehensive digital identity-management and staff-verification framework capable of establishing that individuals presented as employees of an institution were genuinely affiliated with it.
Alausa said the government would explore collaboration with the National Identity Management Commission, NIMC, including the use of the National Identification Number, NIN, alongside other appropriate and secure technologies.
“The objective is straightforward: one individual, one verifiable identity and an accurately declared institutional affiliation,” he said.
He added that the system should be capable of detecting cases where an individual was improperly presented as full-time personnel in more than one institution.
The minister also said the proposed reforms would ensure that the actual composition of academic departments, including junior academic staff and other personnel who genuinely constitute the workforce, was captured digitally.

deduped_items.title: Three western nations move to ban imports of Israeli products from West Bank settlements
deduped_items.summary: Britain, France, and Canada on Tuesday announced measures to ban imports of goods originating from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The three nations said that this aims to support the two-state solution amidst growing international concern over settlement expansion, Reuters reported. The move comes part of a series of measures against Israel’s settlement … The post Three western nations move to ban imports of Israeli products from West Bank settlements appeared first on Egypt Inde
deduped_items.body_text:
Britain, France, and Canada on Tuesday announced measures to ban imports of goods originating from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The three nations said that this aims to support the two-state solution amidst growing international concern over settlement expansion, Reuters reported.
The move comes part of a series of measures against Israel’s settlement policy, and follows as ten other countries have joined a joint statement affirming their commitment to protecting the two-state solution and pursuing a just and lasting peace through negotiations.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said that his country could no longer simply condemn what he described as injustice and suffering, emphasizing the need to take action against settlement expansion—a practice he views as a threat to the viability of a future Palestinian state.
Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand affirmed that settlements in the West Bank undermine efforts to achieve a long-lasting peace based on the two-state solution.
And France said that the acceleration of settlement expansion and escalating violence in the West Bank forced it to take this step.
Backlash from Israel and the US
These measures drew criticism from Israel and the US.
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the expulsion of the British ambassador, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir demanded the closure of the British consulate in East Jerusalem.
These moves coincided with Israel’s announcement of plans to build 1,000 new housing units in the West Bank, amidst growing international concern regarding the “E1” settlement project near Jerusalem—a project viewed one of the most significant threats to the territorial contiguity of Palestinian lands.
Although settlement exports account for only a small fraction of Israel’s total trade, the bans carry political and diplomatic significance, forming part of broader efforts to press for the preservation of the two-state solution.

deduped_items.title: FM, Bahraini counterpart discuss bilateral relations, regional developments over phone
deduped_items.summary: Egypt is exploring the establishment of a local factory to produce alternative soil, aiming to cut imports, lower agricultural production costs and support the expansion of modern, high-value farming and agri-exports. Industry Minister Khaled Hashem had talks with Pekka Tennilä, CEO of Kekkilä-BVB, on the company’s plan to establish a factory in Egypt in partnership … The post FM, Bahraini counterpart discuss bilateral relations, regional developments over phone appeared first on Egypt Independe
deduped_items.body_text:
Egypt is exploring the establishment of a local factory to produce alternative soil, aiming to cut imports, lower agricultural production costs and support the expansion of modern, high-value farming and agri-exports.
Industry Minister Khaled Hashem had talks with Pekka Tennilä, CEO of Kekkilä-BVB, on the company’s plan to establish a factory in Egypt in partnership with Egyptian agritech company Agriventure. The facility is planned for the Suez Canal Economic Zone and will produce alternative growing soil for precision farming.
Hashem said localizing alternative growing-soil production is a strategic priority for supporting modern and protected agriculture and increasing value added in agro-industrial manufacturing.
He added that agricultural manufacturing technologies are among the ministry’s priorities for linking scientific research with industrial outputs, meeting export requirements, reducing production costs and narrowing the import gap.
The minister also highlighted the importance of deploying advanced technologies and innovative solutions across productive activities, particularly those that help conserve water and improve resource efficiency in agriculture.
Such solutions, he said, can support the growth and competitiveness of agro-industrial projects and strengthen their export potential.
Kekkilä-BVB company officials said alternative growing media account for around 30% of the cost of precision farming, underscoring the importance of local production in reducing agricultural costs. The planned factory will serve the domestic market while expanding exports to European, African and Arab markets.
Hashem also said Agriventure could participate in the ministry’s “Productive Village” initiative, particularly in villages with a competitive edge in medicinal and aromatic plants and export-oriented crops.
The initiative aims to support balanced industrial development and curb illegal migration and population movement from the regions by leveraging the comparative advantages of each governorate and village. It includes providing small industrial workshops and complexes, concessional financing for small investors, and technical support to connect small businesses with medium- and large-scale factories and strengthen supply-chain integration.
The minister added that Egypt’s industrial map will help identify the comparative advantages of each village and potentially allocate sites for precision-farming projects, particularly in villages known for producing medicinal and aromatic plants and export-oriented crops.

deduped_items.summary: Britain, France, and Canada on Tuesday announced measures to ban imports of goods originating from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The three nations said that this aims to support the two-state solution amidst growing international concern over settlement expansion, Reuters reported. The move comes part of a series of measures against Israel’s settlement … The post Three western nations move to ban imports of Israeli products from West Bank settlements appeared first on Egypt Inde
deduped_items.body_text:
Britain, France, and Canada on Tuesday announced measures to ban imports of goods originating from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The three nations said that this aims to support the two-state solution amidst growing international concern over settlement expansion, Reuters reported.
The move comes part of a series of measures against Israel’s settlement policy, and follows as ten other countries have joined a joint statement affirming their commitment to protecting the two-state solution and pursuing a just and lasting peace through negotiations.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said that his country could no longer simply condemn what he described as injustice and suffering, emphasizing the need to take action against settlement expansion—a practice he views as a threat to the viability of a future Palestinian state.
Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand affirmed that settlements in the West Bank undermine efforts to achieve a long-lasting peace based on the two-state solution.
And France said that the acceleration of settlement expansion and escalating violence in the West Bank forced it to take this step.
Backlash from Israel and the US
These measures drew criticism from Israel and the US.
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the expulsion of the British ambassador, while National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir demanded the closure of the British consulate in East Jerusalem.
These moves coincided with Israel’s announcement of plans to build 1,000 new housing units in the West Bank, amidst growing international concern regarding the “E1” settlement project near Jerusalem—a project viewed one of the most significant threats to the territorial contiguity of Palestinian lands.
Although settlement exports account for only a small fraction of Israel’s total trade, the bans carry political and diplomatic significance, forming part of broader efforts to press for the preservation of the two-state solution.

Sudan Nashra: Hemedti in Addis Ababa | Buildup at Ethiopian base fuels concerns over RSF corridor toward Blue Nile capital, military sends massive reinforcements | RSF fortifies West Darfur capital with berms, reinforces troops | RSF commander in North Kordofan defects, arrives in capital with 200 fighters          
        When Rapid Support Forces Commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo quietly touched down in Addis Ababa last week, the Blue Nile State front was raging along Ethiopia’s border and reinforcements for the fighting were amassing on both sides. Ethiopia, meanwhile, was contending with renewed tensions of its own.
For the RSF, keeping channels open with Addis Ababa is particularly important given that its border is part of the security environment surrounding the fighting in Blue Nile. Operations and troop movements along the border were among the main subjects of Hemedti’s talks, according to an RSF leadership source and an Ethiopian government source who spoke to Mada Masr. For the Ethiopian source, Addis Ababa’s immediate concern is keeping Sudan’s war from spilling across the border.
But Sudanese intelligence sees another layer to Ethiopia’s interest in the RSF. Ethiopia could factor the paramilitary group into its own military arrangements as it manages conflicts with domestic opponents, particularly amid renewed tensions with Tigray, a Sudanese intelligence source said. Such a relationship could also give Addis Ababa greater room to operate on the Sudanese side of the border, they added.
The Sudanese military is watching that possibility from an increasingly exposed position. It has lost the strategic border towns of Geisan and Kurmuk in Blue Nile and is now trying to stop the advance from the border toward Blue Nile’s capital, Damazin.
And there is a new reason for concern — a significant buildup since July at an Ethiopian military base in Asosa, located in the Benishangul-Gumuz region bordering Sudan. The area has been repeatedly used to launch major operations by the RSF and its allies into Blue Nile. But an intelligence source in the state said the recent buildup could make the cross-border corridor into Kurmuk and Geisan harder for the military to penetrate and could facilitate the unimpeded movement of supplies and forces to the RSF and its allies.
With the border towns secured, the RSF and its allies are now pushing against the military positions guarding Damazin. They captured Bakori in the Geisan locality and Sirkum in Kurmuk last week, triggering a rush of military reinforcements into the state capital and the positions around it.
While the military is shoring up Damazin, the RSF is fortifying Geneina, the capital of West Darfur. Military operations this week secured another position near the city, part of an offensive that has been underway since July and has brought military and allied forces within reach of the RSF-held capital.
The RSF is now digging around the city, extending sand berms and trenches as a defensive measure against a possible surprise attack. This week, it brought in large numbers of fighters in what a military field source described as preparation for attacks on military positions in West Darfur and neighboring North Darfur.
Kordofan, the war’s critical faultline between an RSF push east and a military push west, saw its second major defection this week. Abu Bakr Dahloub, the RSF’s intelligence chief for special missions in North Kordofan’s Hamra al-Sheikh and the Egypt-Libya-Sudan border triangle, defected to the military with around 200 fighters.
After securing major gains in North Kordofan weeks ago, the military continues to target RSF supply and gathering points in neighboring West Kordofan. Military aircraft struck several fuel and ammunition depots and RSF gatherings there this week, destroying supplies that had just arrived to reinforce positions in the area.
In Khartoum, the state is trying to get its internal political dialogue off the ground despite intractable dis

What’s behind the US sanctions on Banque Misr UAE?                    
                For Egyptian officials, the singling out of Banque Misr UAE in American sanctions was shocking, even if there are multiple rationales through which the move could be read.
The announcement of sanctions that came on Friday was the latest move in America’s new strategy to suffocate Iran. In mid August, United States President Donald Trump let it be known that he was fed up. After months of negotiations with Iran over an end to a war, a war that the US and Israel started, had failed to materialize, it was time to change tactics.
This time, it wouldn’t be a new naval blockade on an existing naval blockade. It wouldn’t be more military action. This time, Trump wrote on his social media account, the pain would come in the form of the “MOST CRUSHING ECONOMIC OPERATION EVER TAKEN AGAINST ANY COUNTRY.”
Essentially, the plan, dubbed “Economic D-Day,” a reference to the US invasion of Nazi-held France during World War II, would see Washington DC impose secondary sanctions on any country that “allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran.”
Swooping in to take up the messaging of the plan, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent began to beat the war drum of economic sanctions.
“If you insist on doing business with [Iran], then the US Treasury and U.S. government will put its full might and force against you,” Bessent said on August 20. “It’s time for our allies and the rest of the world to make a decision.”
The media was awash in speculation. Turkey and the United Arab Emirates are among Iran’s largest trade partners. Would the US really consider sanctioning such key allies?
And then the decisive day came. On Friday, the US treasury announced its first salvo.
First to be sanctioned was Reza Mohammad Taeedi, the manager of the Iranian commercial bank Bank Melli’s Dubai branch.
It made sense: an Iranian bank operating in Dubai surely must be part of a shadow banking operation.
Next was Kameng Trading Limited, a Hong Kong-based exchange company that has allegedly helped launder funds for a sanctioned Iranian exchange house.
Again, the proximity to China, which is known to have relations with Iran, made the move legible.
But the last entity included in the sanctions notice was a surprise. The United Arab Emirates branches of Banque Misr, the Egyptian state-owned bank and the second largest in Egypt, holding assets worth US$83 billion, could see its banking access to US financial institutions revoked, the US treasury announced.
Describing the five branches of what is Egypt’s second largest bank, the US treasury note called the bank “a critical node for the Iranian regime’s access to US dollars. Treasury estimates that between January 2024 and June 2026, Banque Misr UAE processed approximately $1.8 billion for 103 companies that are potentially part of Iranian shadow banking networks.”
“Banque Misr UAE’s customers include apparent front companies used by Iran’s Ministry of Defense and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to evade US sanctions, as well as to launder money on behalf of Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei,” the statement read.
The US treasury has given Banque Misr 30 days before the sanctions take effect. In the meantime, it is accepting comments from the public, industry experts and financial institutions about the proposed sanction.
While the reasons are still unknown, the decision did not materialize out of thin air.
Since around 2023, Egypt has faced a new difficult reality.
A $23 billion deal with Saudi Arabia inked in 2016 had expired, and while the initial deal had been greased with the handover of Tiran and Sanafir islands, Egypt and Saudi relations had taken a turn for much rockier shores. deduped_items.body_text:
Who should be in charge of the war?
This article is based upon my experiences in MOD UK and Army and Joint staff during the first Gulf War, Bosnia and with NATO in Kosovo. I turned for support to my US defence academic friend and author Dr Thomas Durell Young a former member of staff at the US war college, and a former Policy Director in MOD Bulgaria Retired Colonel Vladimir Milenski. We all worked variously together with MOD Ukraine in 2014 and 2015 and between us on reform in over 15 other countries worldwide. I apologize in advance to my female military friends for using he throughout this article, but it reflects simplicity of writing before translation not denigration of your amazing contribution to the national war effort.
Introduction: War Does Not Suspend Democratic Defence Governance, it severely tests it
In a democratic state at war, the defence system must be able to fight effectively while remaining politically controlled, legally accountable, strategically coherent and operationally agile. War increases pressure on institutions, but the defence system must not become insular or a power on its own. War does not remove the need for clear authority, lawful responsibility and public accountability. On the contrary, the greater the stakes, the more important it is to know who governs defence, who advises government, who generates forces, who plans strategy and campaigns, who commands operations, and who answers for results. Today this is not totally clear in Ukraine.
The institutional question is therefore not primarily one of terminology. Different democratic states use different titles for organisations and posts. What matters is whether these offices form a coherent system in which authority, responsibility, military advice, operational command, force generation, political control and accountability are clearly separated where necessary and integrated where useful – and most importantly society can see who is in charge and responsible for each task. There is no doubt that to achieve a well-oiled, well-managed system the key requirement is outstanding teamwork. The fastest and best process is always two friends working together with a common purpose. Lack of trust, institutional arrogance, poor teamwork, bureaucracy or unclear tasks lead to delay - and delay kills.
In this regard the Minister and senior commanders, MOD, General Staff (GS) and Joint Staff (JS) must function as a single organism, working closely together not in opposition. I have been lucky to work in a combined MOD/General Staff in UK with teams of officers and civil servants serving together. Meetings contained staff from all relevant HQs from MOD to units and many key decisions could be made and implemented immediately without need for bureaucracy. The civilian component came with different, less narrow thinking and skills, and added to achieving results hugely. Sharing work openly is vastly better than strict ownership.
In Ukraine, the main headquarters are the MOD and the General Staff (GS) (Most countries would call this HQ, Defence Staff as it is more than just army). We suggest a third strand is needed as Joint Staff, which should manage the fighting. UK and many NATO countries have an operational Joint Staff HQ and US have the regional combatant commands (COCOMS) reflecting their world view. Together, these three HQs would form a leadership triangle with clear and separate tasks. I have worked variously at all three levels. Depending on the issue in need of resolution, one headquarters leads the staff work, while the others support it. The next day the task and leadership requirement may be totally different. States that inherit command structures from the Soviet military tradition and then introduce institutions associated with modern democratic and NATO ways of defence management are always challenged in who does what, how and when. The problem is not that one idea, or vocabulary is "Eastern" and another "Western." The problem is that mixed

deduped_items.title: Ukraine Is Facing Another Financing Crisis
deduped_items.summary: Trump has floated demanding repayment for US support to Ukraine, claiming over $300 billion – a figure far exceeding Kiel Institute’s tracked $133 billion. With US aid at zero since 2025, Europe already shoulders most funding, while Ukraine faces a $27-32 billion financing gap this year. Ukraine is meanwhile already facing financial strain. Seizing immobilized Russian central bank assets remains the cleanest fix, but political will is lacking.

deduped_items.title: Метро Москвы продлят в область
deduped_items.body_text:
Московский метрополитен планируют продлить в семь направлений Подмосковья. Об этом завил мэр столицы Сергей Собянин, его слова передает ТАСС.
«По предварительным планам, которые мы наметили с Московской областью, Московский метрополитен выйдет с семью линиями за пределы МКАД и будет обслуживать городские округа, которые находятся вокруг МКАД и составляют примерно треть населения Московской области», — рассказал глава города.
Новые станции построят в Красногорске, Химках, Мытищах, Балашихе, Одинцове и двух направлениях Ленинского округа.
Собянин подчеркнул, что Москва и область образуют единую агломерацию, где проживает 20 миллионов человек. Примерно треть населения Подмосковья сконцентрировано в городских округах вокруг МКАД — именно их и будут обслуживать новые направления метро. Приступить к их планированию и строительству собираются после 2030 года.
Сейчас в Московской области работают всего две станции метро — «Мякинино» Арбатско-Покровской линии и «Котельники» Таганско-Краснопресненской линии.
Еще одной приоритетной задачей мэрии на следующее десятилетие остается строительство метро в Новой Москве, включая Щербинку. Благодаря появлению в районе новых станций транспортная доступность улучшится для более чем 5,7 миллиона москвичей и жителей области.

deduped_items.title: Украинские театры выразили желание выступать в России
deduped_items.body_text:
Начальник отдела гастрольных программ Росконцерта Владимир Черкасов заявил, что украинские театры выражали желание вернуться на российские площадки. Об этом он рассказал в интервью ТАСС.
Черкасов отметил, что сейчас зарубежные контакты ограничены странами СНГ. Ранее в этот список входила и Украина.
«Сейчас по известным причинам Украина не принимает участия, хотя мы получаем информацию такую, что многие театры хотели бы вернуться на российские площадки», — сообщил он.
Представитель Росконцерта также высказался о прекращении работы с прибалтийскими странами. По его словам, Росконцерт пока не планирует расширять количество партнеров.
Ранее актер Театра Вахтангова Иван Захава заявил, что отправится в зону специальной военной операции (СВО). Захава добавил, что этот вопрос является для него личным, «сидящим глубоко в душе».

deduped_items.title: Бейонсе отметила 45-летие в наряде за 1,2 миллиона рублей
deduped_items.body_text:
Американская певица Бейонсе отметила юбилей в роскошном наряде. Его стоимость раскрыло Page Six.
Исполнительница пришла на вечеринку в Лондоне по случаю 45-летия с матерью Тиной Ноулз и мужем, рэпером Jay-Z. Бейонсе появилась в золотисто-бронзовом образе, который состоял из отделанной бахромой из бисера микро-юбки Roberto Cavalli за 2395 долларов (205 тысяч рублей) и топа из прозрачного шифона с бархатной отделкой за 2995 долларов (257 тысяч рублей).
Бейонсе дополнила образ золотой сумкой Jimmy Choo стоимостью 8495 долларов (728 тысяч рублей) и красными солнцезащитными очками того же бренда за 505 долларов (43 тысячи рублей). Общая стоимость всех изделий составила 1,2 миллиона рублей.
В мае в сети уличили Бейонсе в использовании фотошопа на снимках с Met Gala. Тогда фанаты заявили, что на фотографиях в собственных соцсетях певица выглядела иначе, чем на кадрах, размещенных в изданиях.

deduped_items.title: Путин принял в Кремле лидера Вьетнама
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Путин принимает участие в церемонии официальной встречи лидера Вьетнама То Лама в Кремле.
- Церемония проходит в Георгиевском зале Большого Кремлевского дворца.
МОСКВА, 9 сен - РИА Новости. Президент России Владимир Путин в среду принимает участие в церемонии официальной встречи лидера Вьетнама То Лама, которая проходит в Кремле, передает корреспондент РИА Новости. 
Торжественная церемония проходит в Георгиевском зале Большого Кремлевского дворца. 
В ходе церемонии официальной встречи главы государств приветствуют друг друга, звучат государственные гимны. Затем лидеры представляют делегации двух стран.

deduped_items.title: Президент Вьетнама прибыл в Кремль на переговоры с Путиным
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Президент Вьетнама То Лам прибыл в Кремль на переговоры с Владимиром Путиным.
- Ожидается, что они обсудят состояние и перспективы развития стратегического партнерства, а также примут пакет двусторонних документов.
МОСКВА, 9 сен - РИА Новости. Президент Вьетнама То Лам в среду прибыл в Кремль на переговоры с президентом России Владимиром Путиным, передает корреспондент РИА Новости. 
На предстоящих переговорах Путин и То Лам планируют обсудить состояние и перспективы дальнейшего развития российско-вьетнамского всеобъемлющего стратегического партнерства. Среди основных тем - торгово-экономические и научно-образовательные связи, гуманитарные обмены, взаимодействие в областях безопасности и обороны. Также состоится обмен мнениями по актуальным вопросам международной и региональной повестки дня. 
По итогам переговоров планируется принять пакет двусторонних документов.

deduped_items.title: Эксперт Минздрава рассказал, при каких условиях можно оказать первую помощь
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Главный внештатный специалист по первой помощи Минздрава России Андрей Колодкин сообщил, что для оказания первой помощи пострадавшему необходимы внутренняя готовность, аптечка и телефон на громкой связи.
- В случае несчастного случая можно позвонить по телефону «103», и диспетчер подскажет последовательность действий.
- В России активно развивается система дистанционного консультирования очевидцев несчастного случая по оказанию первой помощи в режиме онлайн.
МОСКВА, 9 сен - РИА Новости. Первую помощь пострадавшему в результате несчастного случая можно оказать в случае наличия внутренней готовности, аптечки и медика на громкой связи, сообщил главный внештатный специалист по первой помощи Минздрава России, заместитель председателя Российского общества первой помощи Андрей Колодкин. 
Пресс-конференция, посвященная развитию навыков оказания первой помощи в России, прошла в среду в Международном мультимедицном пресс-центре "Россия сегодня". 
Мурашко рассказал об оперативности скорой помощи
18 июня, 12:59
"Главное - наша собственная внутренняя готовность и наличие средств индивидуальной защиты, то есть любой аптечке первой помощи, где есть перчатки и средства оказания первой помощи, и, собственно, телефон на громкой связи", - сказал Колодкин. 
Он уточнил, что в случае, если человек стал свидетелем несчастного случая и готов оказать первую помощь, можно позвонить по телефону "103", тогда диспетчера подскажут последовательность действий. 
"У нас в стране активно развивается система дистанционного консультирования очевидцев несчастного случая по оказанию первой помощи в режиме онлайн, когда диспетчер действительно подскажет ход и последовательность действий", - заключил эксперт.

deduped_items.title: Martina Carbonaro, la mamma depone con il braccialetto elettronico. “Lei morta, lui tranquillo”
deduped_items.summary: La deposizione di Fiorenza Cossentino, colpita col marito dal divieto di avvicinamento ai parenti dell’imputato Alessio Tucci: “Lui sapeva che mia figlia non c’era più ma si mostrava tranquillo. Fece persino il caffè ai carabinieri”. In aula anche l’amica con cui la vittima trascorse le ultime ore di vita: “Era arrabbiata perché non l’amava più ma lui voleva riallacciare il rapporto a tutti i costi”

deduped_items.body_text:
Víctor Sánchez y Salim El Jebari regresan al trabajo con el Córdoba CF y apuntan a estar presentes ante el Almería
El conjunto blanquiverde volvió al trabajo con el objetivo de sacudirse las dudas ante el Almería en una sesión que dejó nuevos avances en la recuperación de Adilson
Córdoba
El Córdoba CF busca pasar página de inmediato. Tras la derrota ante el Sabadell, la segunda consecutiva, el conjunto blanquiverde regresó este miércoles al trabajo con la vista puesta en la visita del Almería el próximo sábado a El Arcángel (21.00 horas). ... Los pupulos de Iván Ania afrontan una semana marcada por la necesidad de corregir su fragilidad defensiva y recuperar sensaciones después de un arranque irregular.
La primera sesión de la semana dejó dos novedades importantes en la plantilla del Córdoba CF. Víctor Sánchez y Salim El Jebari volvieron a ejercitarse junto al grupo y completaron el entrenamiento con total normalidad. Un paso adelante en sus respectivas recuperaciones que aumenta sus opciones de estar disponibles para el duelo ante el Almería, a falta todavía de dos sesiones antes del encuentro.
Especialmente significativa fue la presencia de Salim El Jebari. El extremo hispano-marroquí completó por primera vez una sesión íntegra junto a sus compañeros desde su llegada al Córdoba. El atacante aterrizó en El Arcángel arrastrando unas molestias en el pubis que le han impedido participar con normalidad desde el inicio de la pretemporada. Por la complejidad de este tipo de dolencias, el club ha manejado su recuperación con cautela hasta que este miércoles pudo completar diferentes cargas de intensidad sin contratiempos y al ritmo de sus compañeros.
Noticia relacionada
También dio un paso importante Víctor Sánchez. El atacante sevillano, goleador en su debut ante el Girona, se perdió los dos últimos encuentros frente al Granada y el Sabadell por una lesión de bajo grado en el aductor. Después de realizar trabajo con balón al margen durante la pasada semana, completó su primer entrenamiento con el grupo desde la lesión y dejó buenas sensaciones, especialmente de cara a portería, tras cerca de dos semanas de ausencia.
Todo ello en una sesión que comenzó en un ambiente distendido. Los pupilos de Iván Ania llegaron a la Ciudad Deportiva entre bromas antes de saltar al campo anexo, escenario provisional de los entrenamientos mientras el terreno de juego principal se encuentra inmerso en el proceso de sustitución del césped.
Adilson sigue progresando en su recuperación
Ania contó con todos los efectivos disponibles del primer equipo, incluido el flamante fichaje Nélson Monte, y sin presencia de jugadores del filial y las bajas de larga duración de Fomeyem y Jacobo Martí. El buen ambiente, sin embargo, no restó seriedad ni concentración al trabajo. El Córdoba es consciente de las dudas generadas en este arranque de temporada y quiere despejarlas de un plumazo ante el Almería, en una cita que se presenta como un importante termómetro para medir la reacción blanquiverde, dar un golpe sobre la mesa y tratar de relanzar el vuelo tras dos derrotas consecutivas.
Con este objetivo en mente, la sesión arrancó con diferentes ejercicios de activación y conducción con balón antes de dar paso al trabajo de posesión en espacios reducidos e ir aumentado progresivamente la intensidad para meter en dinámica a todo el plantel.
Tras un breve receso y varios minutos de trote, con una carga algo menor para los futbolistas que partieron como titulares ante el Sabadell, llegó el turno del partidillo. Los pupilos de Iván Ania elevaron el ritmo al máximo en un ejercicio muy exigente que también dejó otra imagen destacada, la presencia de Adilson sobre el césped.
El extremo portugués ya pisa césped y realiza ejercicios de acondicionamiento con balón, un paso más dentro de una recuperación que sigue desarrollándose con cautela. Su presencia sobre el terreno de juego, sin embargo, no implica que su regreso esté próximo. Los plazos continúan siendo largos y no será

deduped_items.summary: El Gobierno de Castilla-La Mancha ha aprobado ayudas por un importe conjunto de 1,4 millones de euros para actuaciones de conservación y mejora de dos de los principales conjuntos patrimoniales de la provincia de Toledo: el castillo de Escalona y los molinos de viento de Consuegra. Según ha informado la consejera Portavoz del Gobierno regional, Esther Padilla, este miércoles en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Gobierno, la actuación contempla una ayuda de 200.000 euros para las obras d
deduped_items.body_text:
CASTILLA-LA MANCHA
La Junta destina 1,4 millones a recuperar el castillo de Escalona y los molinos de Consuegra
El Gobierno regional aportará 200.000 euros para el castillo y 1,2 millones para restaurar e iluminar el conjunto de Consuegra
Toledo
El Gobierno de Castilla-La Mancha ha aprobado ayudas por un importe conjunto de 1,4 millones de euros para actuaciones de conservación y mejora de dos de los principales conjuntos patrimoniales de la provincia de Toledo: el castillo de Escalona y los molinos ... de viento de Consuegra.
Según ha informado la consejera Portavoz del Gobierno regional, Esther Padilla, este miércoles en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Gobierno, la actuación contempla una ayuda de 200.000 euros para las obras de reconstrucción del castillo de Escalona, después del derrumbe que sufrió parte de la fortaleza el pasado mes de marzo y que provocó daños materiales.
200.000
euros
Reconstrucción del castillo de Escalona después del derrumbe de una torre el pasado mes de marzo
Tras el incidente, técnicos de Patrimonio se desplazaron hasta el municipio toledano para evaluar los elementos afectados y comprobar también el estado del resto del edificio. La ayuda permitirá intervenir en la zona dañada y avanzar en la conservación de una fortaleza que fue adquirida por el Ayuntamiento de Escalona en 2024.
Noticia relacionada
En el caso de Consuegra, el Ejecutivo autonómico ha aprobado una ayuda de 194.000 euros para la restauración de los molinos de viento situados en el cerro Calderico. Los trabajos permitirán reparar los daños ocasionados a finales de enero por un temporal de viento que alcanzó rachas de hasta 90 kilómetros por hora. Seis molinos resultaron afectados: dos sufrieron importantes daños en sus aspas, mientras que otros cuatro registraron desperfectos en las cubiertas y los ejes.
194.000
euros
Restauración de los molinos de viento afectados por un temporal el pasado mes de enero
Los daños obligaron a restringir temporalmente el acceso al cerro Calderico y tuvieron también consecuencias sobre el desarrollo habitual de las actividades turísticas del municipio.
La portavoz del Gobierno regional ha recordado que los molinos de Consuegra están declarados Bien de Interés Cultural (BIC) y constituyen «una de las imágenes más reconocibles de Castilla-La Mancha dentro y fuera de nuestra región».
Un millón para la iluminación
A la restauración se suma una inversión de un millón de euros para renovar la iluminación ornamental del castillo y los molinos de Consuegra, un compromiso adquirido por el presidente regional, Emiliano García-Page, con el municipio. La actuación se ejecutará entre 2026 y 2027 y supondrá sustituir el actual sistema de iluminación por tecnología LED de alta eficiencia, además de incorporar un sistema de gestión inteligente.
1.000.000
euros
Renovación de la iluminación ornamental del castillo y de los molinos de Consuegra
El proyecto contempla la instalación de 187 proyectores, de los que 92 estarán destinados al castillo y otros 95 a las fachadas de los 12 molinos. También se colocarán 49 balizas a lo largo de todo el recorrido.
Padilla ha destacado la importancia turística del conjunto, señalando que Consuegra recibió el pasado año más de 15.000 visitantes al mes. La nueva iluminación permitirá mejorar todavía más la imagen nocturna de uno de los principales reclamos patrimoniales y turísticos de la provincia de Toledo.

deduped_items.body_text:
Víctor Sánchez y Salim El Jebari regresan al trabajo con el Córdoba CF y apuntan a estar presentes ante el Almería
El conjunto blanquiverde volvió al trabajo con el objetivo de sacudirse las dudas ante el Almería en una sesión que dejó nuevos avances en la recuperación de Adilson
Córdoba
El Córdoba CF busca pasar página de inmediato. Tras la derrota ante el Sabadell, la segunda consecutiva, el conjunto blanquiverde regresó este miércoles al trabajo con la vista puesta en la visita del Almería el próximo sábado a El Arcángel (21.00 horas). ... Los pupulos de Iván Ania afrontan una semana marcada por la necesidad de corregir su fragilidad defensiva y recuperar sensaciones después de un arranque irregular.
La primera sesión de la semana dejó dos novedades importantes en la plantilla del Córdoba CF. Víctor Sánchez y Salim El Jebari volvieron a ejercitarse junto al grupo y completaron el entrenamiento con total normalidad. Un paso adelante en sus respectivas recuperaciones que aumenta sus opciones de estar disponibles para el duelo ante el Almería, a falta todavía de dos sesiones antes del encuentro.
Especialmente significativa fue la presencia de Salim El Jebari. El extremo hispano-marroquí completó por primera vez una sesión íntegra junto a sus compañeros desde su llegada al Córdoba. El atacante aterrizó en El Arcángel arrastrando unas molestias en el pubis que le han impedido participar con normalidad desde el inicio de la pretemporada. Por la complejidad de este tipo de dolencias, el club ha manejado su recuperación con cautela hasta que este miércoles pudo completar diferentes cargas de intensidad sin contratiempos y al ritmo de sus compañeros.
Noticia relacionada
También dio un paso importante Víctor Sánchez. El atacante sevillano, goleador en su debut ante el Girona, se perdió los dos últimos encuentros frente al Granada y el Sabadell por una lesión de bajo grado en el aductor. Después de realizar trabajo con balón al margen durante la pasada semana, completó su primer entrenamiento con el grupo desde la lesión y dejó buenas sensaciones, especialmente de cara a portería, tras cerca de dos semanas de ausencia.
Todo ello en una sesión que comenzó en un ambiente distendido. Los pupilos de Iván Ania llegaron a la Ciudad Deportiva entre bromas antes de saltar al campo anexo, escenario provisional de los entrenamientos mientras el terreno de juego principal se encuentra inmerso en el proceso de sustitución del césped.
Adilson sigue progresando en su recuperación
Ania contó con todos los efectivos disponibles del primer equipo, incluido el flamante fichaje Nélson Monte, y sin presencia de jugadores del filial y las bajas de larga duración de Fomeyem y Jacobo Martí. El buen ambiente, sin embargo, no restó seriedad ni concentración al trabajo. El Córdoba es consciente de las dudas generadas en este arranque de temporada y quiere despejarlas de un plumazo ante el Almería, en una cita que se presenta como un importante termómetro para medir la reacción blanquiverde, dar un golpe sobre la mesa y tratar de relanzar el vuelo tras dos derrotas consecutivas.
Con este objetivo en mente, la sesión arrancó con diferentes ejercicios de activación y conducción con balón antes de dar paso al trabajo de posesión en espacios reducidos e ir aumentado progresivamente la intensidad para meter en dinámica a todo el plantel.
Tras un breve receso y varios minutos de trote, con una carga algo menor para los futbolistas que partieron como titulares ante el Sabadell, llegó el turno del partidillo. Los pupilos de Iván Ania elevaron el ritmo al máximo en un ejercicio muy exigente que también dejó otra imagen destacada, la presencia de Adilson sobre el césped.
El extremo portugués ya pisa césped y realiza ejercicios de acondicionamiento con balón, un paso más dentro de una recuperación que sigue desarrollándose con cautela. Su presencia sobre el terreno de juego, sin embargo, no implica que su regreso esté próximo. Los plazos continúan siendo largos y no será

deduped_items.body_text:
Prague Unemployment Reaches 4% with 40,509 Job Seekers
Prague Morning
Unemployment in Prague rises to 4% at the end of August, with 40,509 people registered as job seekers at the Labour Office.
The figure was 2.1% higher than in July and 15.7% higher than a year earlier.
Despite the increase, Prague continued to record the lowest unemployment rate among Czechia’s regions. The national unemployment rate stood at 5% at the end of August.
More people registered as job seekers
A total of 5,368 people registered with the Prague Labour Office in August. That was 133 fewer than in July but 1,033 more than in August 2025.
At the end of August, Prague had 37,811 people considered reachable for employment. This category covers people aged 15 to 64 who are not temporarily unable to work and are not taking part in retraining.
The number of reachable job seekers increased by 822 compared with July and by 5,475 compared with the same month last year.
Women accounted for 55.2% of all registered job seekers, with 22,378 women listed in the Labour Office records.
More than 22,000 vacancies remain available
Employers in Prague had 22,519 registered vacancies at the end of August. That was 708 fewer positions than in July and 565 fewer than a year earlier.
There were an average of 1.8 registered job seekers for every vacancy.
Of the total number of registered vacancies, 1,676 were not marked as positions available to foreign workers. Employers could recruit workers from abroad for a further 20,843 positions.
Construction, accommodation and food services, and wholesale and retail were among the sectors with the largest number of vacancies.

AIGEL to Celebrate 10th Anniversary with Prague Concert
Prague Morning
On October 21, electronic duo AIGEL will perform at Futurum Music Bar in Prague as part of a special concert marking the band’s 10th anniversary.
AIGEL was formed by Tatar poet and singer Aigel Gaisina and St. Petersburg producer Ilya Baramiya. Over the past decade, the duo has developed a distinctive sound combining electronic music, trip-hop and psychedelic influences.
Their music crosses linguistic and cultural boundaries, with songs performed in Russian, Tatar, English and German.
AIGEL gained international attention with the viral tracks “Tatarin” and “Pyyala.” The latter topped streaming charts in 25 countries and reached No. 1 on the global Shazam chart.
Over 10 years, the duo has released five albums and dozens of singles. They have also received a Cannes Lion for the music video “You’re Born” and toured extensively across Europe and beyond.
Now based in Europe, AIGEL is preparing a special anniversary show in Prague, combining the duo’s electronic sound with Gaisina’s distinctive and expressive vocals.
The concert will take place on October 21 at Futurum Music Bar.

deduped_items.summary: Michele Cervone d’Urso, the EU’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, raised concerns over Georgia, recalling its obligation to “uphold fundamental freedoms” and urging the “repeal or substantial revision” of legislation that undermines human rights and targets dissent. “The EU recalls Georgia’s obligation to uphold fundamental freedoms and urges the repeal or substantial revision of recent legislation …
deduped_items.body_text:
EU Representative Raises Human Rights, Justice Concerns Over Georgia at UN
Michele Cervone d’Urso, the EU’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, raised concerns over Georgia, recalling its obligation to “uphold fundamental freedoms” and urging the “repeal or substantial revision” of legislation that undermines human rights and targets dissent.
“The EU recalls Georgia’s obligation to uphold fundamental freedoms and urges the repeal or substantial revision of recent legislation that undermines international human rights standards,” Cervone d’Urso said while speaking at the 63rd session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva.
The EU representative said the bloc is “deeply concerned” by what he described as the “politically motivated use of the justice system against civil society organisations” and the adoption of “repressive measures targeting opposition figures, human rights defenders, and independent media.”
He added that the EU “strongly condemns arbitrary arrests and increasing repression,” including “the imprisonment of opposition leaders, independent journalists, media workers, and civil society actors.”
Cervone d’Urso emphasized the need for Georgia to “address these issues, align its policies with international standards, and engage in constructive dialogue to restore trust in its democratic institutions.”
The relations between Georgia, which became an EU candidate country in 2023, and Brussels worsened amid the Georgian Dream government’s anti-democratic moves and anti-EU discourse. The EU said in November 2025 that Georgia is a candidate country “in name only” and moved to suspend visa-free travel for Georgian holders of diplomatic and service passports.

deduped_items.summary: Michele Cervone d’Urso, the EU’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, raised concerns over Georgia, recalling its obligation to “uphold fundamental freedoms” and urging the “repeal or substantial revision” of legislation that undermines human rights and targets dissent. “The EU recalls Georgia’s obligation to uphold fundamental freedoms and urges the repeal or substantial revision of recent legislation …
deduped_items.body_text:
EU Representative Raises Human Rights, Justice Concerns Over Georgia at UN
Michele Cervone d’Urso, the EU’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the UN, raised concerns over Georgia, recalling its obligation to “uphold fundamental freedoms” and urging the “repeal or substantial revision” of legislation that undermines human rights and targets dissent.
“The EU recalls Georgia’s obligation to uphold fundamental freedoms and urges the repeal or substantial revision of recent legislation that undermines international human rights standards,” Cervone d’Urso said while speaking at the 63rd session of the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva.
The EU representative said the bloc is “deeply concerned” by what he described as the “politically motivated use of the justice system against civil society organisations” and the adoption of “repressive measures targeting opposition figures, human rights defenders, and independent media.”
He added that the EU “strongly condemns arbitrary arrests and increasing repression,” including “the imprisonment of opposition leaders, independent journalists, media workers, and civil society actors.”
Cervone d’Urso emphasized the need for Georgia to “address these issues, align its policies with international standards, and engage in constructive dialogue to restore trust in its democratic institutions.”
The relations between Georgia, which became an EU candidate country in 2023, and Brussels worsened amid the Georgian Dream government’s anti-democratic moves and anti-EU discourse. The EU said in November 2025 that Georgia is a candidate country “in name only” and moved to suspend visa-free travel for Georgian holders of diplomatic and service passports.

deduped_items.title: Why is Berlin failing to build more bike lanes?
deduped_items.summary: Berlin had millions available for cycling projects last year but only spent a fraction of its budget. With less than six percent of a planned bike network completed since 2017, here’s how local politics have put the brakes on a more bikeable capital.
deduped_items.body_text:
Recent arrivals from the UK or the US might think Berlin is already bike-friendly, but the German capital is far from meeting its own ambitions for making the city more bikeable.
These are set down in a legally binding plan and supported with dedicated funding and clear targets. Yet the latest figures show the city moving further away from its goals rather than closer to them.
According to the Senate’s latest progress report, around €82.4 million was available for cycling infrastructure in 2025 but only about €27 million was actually spent.
At the same time, just 21.2 kilometres of new cycling infrastructure were completed, down from 32.4 kilometres in 2022 and continuing a three-year decline.
Of the roughly 2,400 kilometre cycling network envisaged for Berlin by 2030, only a little over 140 kilometres had been completed between 2017 and 2025 – or around 5.8 percent of the planned total according to official figures.
Why is so little being built when the money exists and the targets are legally binding?
The answer lies in a long-running political struggle over the future of Berlin's streets – and one which has become a battleground ahead of this month's state election.
READ ALSO: 'No promises' - Decoding the political slogans plastered all over Berlin
How Berlin promised itself a cycling revolution
As with the Deutsche Wohnen & Co Enteignen campaign, citizens' initiatives sometimes deliver results in Berlin which the city’s elected representatives are reluctant to put into practice.
The roots of today's dispute lie in the Fahrradentscheid, a grassroots campaign launched by cycling activists in the mid-2010s. Given its strong public support, Berlin politicians chose not to force a citywide vote and instead incorporated many of the campaign's demands into the city's Mobility Act, which was passed in 2018.
The law created a legal framework for transforming how people move around the city. It was followed by the Cycling Plan, which specified standards and targets for a connected citywide cycling network of roughly 2,400 kilometres to be completed by 2030.
The plan includes protected cycle lanes on major roads, priority routes across the city, safer junctions and better bicycle parking.
The intention was not only to make cycling safer, but also to encourage people to switch some journeys from cars to bikes.
INTERVIEW: How being hit by a car in Berlin revealed the 'scariness' of German bureaucracy
Change of government
The political climate in Berlin changed in 2023 when a CDU-SPD (Black-Red) coalition took power in the capital. Soon after taking office, then transport senator Manja Schreiner (CDU) ordered a review of cycling projects.
In June 2023, district authorities were instructed to freeze projects involving the loss of parking spaces or road lanes, or extensive new 30 km/h zones while the new administration developed different criteria for assessing transport projects.
Later that year, the Senate began replacing the blanket pause with new guidelines that placed greater emphasis on maintaining road capacity for cars, commercial traffic and deliveries.
The decision triggered fierce criticism from cycling organisations and opposition politicians.
Speaking in June 2023, Changing Cities activist Ragnhild Sørensen accused the new administration of looking backwards rather than forwards. The ADFC cycling association argued that the Mobility Act already established clear priorities and standards, making the review unnecessary.
Schreiner defended the changes by arguing that Berlin needed to balance the needs of all road users. She said major roads needed to remain capable of handling commuter, commercial and delivery traffic.
The initial freeze and subsequent review process have created a backlog, which is one reason why funds available for cycling improvements aren’t being converted into completed projects.

deduped_items.body_text:
College students can get a year of Google AI Plus for free
MANILA, Philippines – Google is offering college students in the Philippines a one-year free subscription to Google’s AI Plus Plan.
Google AI Plus includes Study Notebooks, direct access to Gemini Omni, a personalized Daily Brief, Gemini Live, and 400 GB of cloud storage across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos.
With Study Notebooks, students can upload their class materials to have Gemini create a step-by-step study plan. Guides and practice tests can be generated while important dates like exams and deadlines will directly be integrated into Google Calendar.
Meanwhile, Gemini’s interactive visualizations can help students generate 3d simulations to further understand topics. This can range from visual understanding of tables or grids for various math problems, science topics, and more.
RELATED STORY: Smart Device Link allows one number for phone and Apple Watch
How to avail the plan
Eligible students of college and universities in the country can claim the offer by visiting Google’s student hub.
Click on the student plan, then fill in your details for verification.
Students can only avail the offer until December 31, 2026.

Carlos Alcaraz says ‘I leave with a smile’ after epic US Open loss
NEW YORK — At the end, when five riveting sets and one agonizingly tight tiebreak were over — and when the latest-finishing match in U.S. Open history had concluded — Ben Shelton was not the only player smiling.
Carlos Alcaraz, the player Shelton had just defeated in an entertaining, spine-tingling marathon, was smiling too.
READ: Ben Shelton ends Carlos Alcaraz’s US Open title reign
The dethroned defending champ grinned as he walked to the net to hug Shelton. And he did so again a few minutes later when he stood in a hallway surrounded by reporters, reflecting on a night that seemed to have taken every ounce of his strength to endure.
“I leave the court happy,” Alcaraz said. “I leave the court with a smile. I am proud of myself, how I fought.”
There was probably not a single person in Arthur Ashe Stadium who would have disagreed.
Though many of the thousands of fans who remained until the 3:33 a.m. conclusion – yes, you read that time right – cheered for Shelton, the top-ranked American who now meets compatriot Frances Tiafoe in the semis, there were plenty who cheered for Alcaraz, one of the most charismatic players of his or any generation, and one of the most naturally gifted players ever born.
“Ole, Ole Ole Ole,” Alcaraz’s fans chanted, and “Vamos Carlos!” — competing with shouts of “USA, USA” or just “Let’s Go Ben!”
Most importantly, Alcaraz said he was leaving healthy. That had been a real concern going into this U.S. Open after a four-month break due to a wrist injury.
“As I said before the tournament began, my expectation was to go there, compete, play these kind of matches, be healthy,” he said after his 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) defeat.
“I mean it was close, it really was close, so I was disappointed I didn’t get the win in the end, but I’m just happy … physically I was really tired, but I found a way to push myself.”
READ: Returning Carlos Alcaraz vows to take more breaks
The Spaniard also had nothing but praise for Shelton, who played the match of his young career to defeat the seven-time Grand Slam champion.
“Shelton played a very complete, very mature match,” Alcaraz said in Spanish. “He knew exactly what to do at every moment. And, physically, he’s a beast. It seemed like he had no weaknesses whatsoever. “
“It was a war,” Shelton said. “Carlos is one of the greatest champions of our sport. It was the most enjoyable match I’ve had in my career, for sure.”
Alcaraz had arrived at the U.S. Open with much uncertainty as to how much of a liability his wrist injury remained.
READ: Returning Carlos Alcaraz expects to be himself at US Open
But he seemed healthy from the start, and said he felt better than expected. In his first four rounds he lost only one set.
“It feels like I’ve been competing the whole time,” he said of his extended break. “I surprise myself the way that I’m feeling, and the way that I’m recovering after every match. I’m just really happy about it,” he had said after advancing to the fourth round, “that I’m able to perform at my best after every match.”
Alcaraz also said he’d be taking more long breaks in the future, since he didn’t need to depend on a rhythm or to play a lot of tournaments. And he was so relaxed, he didn’t even know, after handily defeating Tommy Paul in his fourth-round match, who he’d be facing next. Former U.S. Open champ Andy Roddick, a commentator for ESPN, let him know.
Then came Tuesday’s (and Wednesday’s) quarterfinals, and Shelton. After Alcaraz won the first, tight set, Shelton started playing out of his mind. He took the next two sets. Alcaraz rallied for the fourth, and then the two traded games in a nerve-wracking fifth.
Among those in the crowd cheering for Alcaraz were Anushka Sancheti and Prajakti Kapde. The two friends, both 28, had traveled to attend together — Sancheti from Atlanta, and Kapde from Raleigh, North Carolina.

deduped_items.body_text:
Antique seeks to preserve legacy of local heroes
SAN JOSE DE BUENAVISTA, Antique — The provincial government of Antique seeks to preserve the legacy of its local heroes by dedicating a hall at its old capitol building and publishing reading materials about their lives.
The Provincial Development Council, during its third quarter meeting on Wednesday, approved the inclusion of P3 million budget in the Supplemental Annual Investment Program No. 4 for the initiatives.
“We will be putting up a heroes hall and publication of reading materials to recognize and perpetuate the heroism of Antique’s local heroes,” said Board Member Vincent Piccio in an interview.
The reading materials will be distributed in schools, municipal and provincial libraries, he added.
The Heroes Hall will be placed beside the space reserved for the National Museum of the Philippines to house the memorabilia and artifacts of the local heroes.
“The Old Antique Capitol will then become a one-stop shop where the National Museum of the Philippines-Antique and the Heroes Hall would be located,” Piccio said.
Piccio said they are now coordinating with the National Historical Commission of the Philippines for the list of local heroes.
Meanwhile, he said the 127-year-old Philippine Revolutionary Flag will be installed at the heroes hall on Oct. 27, 2026, during the “Pagtugyan” (entrusting) ceremony.
The installation also marked the first year since it was turned over to the provincial government last year.
National Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro and Armed Forces of the Philippines chief of staff Gen. Antonio Nafarrete are among the dignitaries invited to grace the occasion. /apl

deduped_items.body_text:
College students can get a year of Google AI Plus for free
MANILA, Philippines – Google is offering college students in the Philippines a one-year free subscription to Google’s AI Plus Plan.
Google AI Plus includes Study Notebooks, direct access to Gemini Omni, a personalized Daily Brief, Gemini Live, and 400 GB of cloud storage across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos.
With Study Notebooks, students can upload their class materials to have Gemini create a step-by-step study plan. Guides and practice tests can be generated while important dates like exams and deadlines will directly be integrated into Google Calendar.
Meanwhile, Gemini’s interactive visualizations can help students generate 3d simulations to further understand topics. This can range from visual understanding of tables or grids for various math problems, science topics, and more.
RELATED STORY: Smart Device Link allows one number for phone and Apple Watch
How to avail the plan
Eligible students of college and universities in the country can claim the offer by visiting Google’s student hub.
Click on the student plan, then fill in your details for verification.
Students can only avail the offer until December 31, 2026.

deduped_items.title: Indonesia airports reopen after Anak Krakatau ash, but Ili Lewotolok plume extends travel disruption
deduped_items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 9 — Volcanic ash from three more Indonesian volcanoes was reported across parts of the archipelago o...
deduped_items.body_text:
JAKARTA, Sept 9 — Volcanic ash from three more Indonesian volcanoes was reported across parts of the archipelago on Wednesday, in addition to Mount Anak Krakatau, with ash from one of them continuing to disrupt air travel in East Nusa Tenggara.
The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said analysis of Himawari-9 satellite imagery at 7am detected volcanic ash from Mount Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara and Mount Dukono and Mount Ibu in North Maluku, alongside ash from Anak Krakatau in the Sunda Strait.
Of the four volcanoes, BMKG said ash from Ili Lewotolok, located on Lembata Island in East Nusa Tenggara in eastern Indonesia, was observed at the highest altitude of up to 8,000 feet (about 2,438 metres), moving northwest to north across parts of Lembata Regency and the Flores Strait.
“The public is urged not to panic, but to remain vigilant, continue monitoring information on volcanic ash distribution and refer to verified information from official sources,” the agency said in its latest post on social media.
Volcanic ash from Ili Lewotolok forced Wunopito Airport in Lewoleba to temporarily close on Tuesday, with the closure subsequently extended until an estimated 7am local time on Thursday, according to state-owned air navigation service provider AirNav Indonesia.
Meanwhile, all eight airports that have been temporarily closed since Sunday due to volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau had reopened by Tuesday, including Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Indonesia’s main international gateway.
Separately, Lampung’s Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD) said a monitoring operation at 10am by the Indonesian Navy vessel KRI Lepu-861 found that eruptive activity at Anak Krakatau remained observable, marked by smoke and volcanic ash.
The agency said the monitoring, which also drew on Himawari-9 satellite imagery, detected ash reaching up to 7,000 feet (about 2,134 metres) and moving northwest, covering part of Lampung Bay. — Bernama

deduped_items.title: FlightRadar24 reports 177 cancellations, cyberattack ruled out as UK travellers suffer ongoing chaos
deduped_items.summary: LONDON, Sept 9 — UK air travellers faced more misery Wednesday with 177 flights scrapped across the country, as Br...
deduped_items.body_text:
LONDON, Sept 9 — UK air travellers faced more misery Wednesday with 177 flights scrapped across the country, as Britain’s air traffic control service scrambled to recover from a technical glitch which it ruled out as a cyberattack.
Aircraft tracking website FlightRadar24 revealed the fresh cancellations after 1,300 flights to and from UK airports were axed Tuesday, with tens of thousands of customers affected at British Airways alone.
Nearly all the latest flights were at London Heathrow, Britain’s busiest airport, FlightRadar24 wrote on X.
The head of the National Air Traffic Services (NATS), Martin Rolfe, meanwhile said “we have at this point ruled out cyber” as a cause.
“We don’t believe it was a cyberattack,” he told BBC Radio.
Rolfe said NATS will be doing a “very, very thorough” investigation into what exactly caused the incident.
NATS warned in an X post late Tuesday that “it will take time to recover” from the outage.
UK news outlets reported that British Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander had summoned Rolfe to a meeting with her on Wednesday.
Rolfe earlier told Sky News that he accepted “full responsibility” but declined to say if he was considering quitting his job.
Alexander said on X that she was “seeking assurances that lessons will be learned and systems that support aviation are up to the job”.
Neal McMahon, chief operations officer at Irish no-frills airline Ryanair, called for Rolfe to be fired, accusing him of having “failed UK travellers”.
‘Knock-on impact’
Heathrow said late Tuesday that departures had resumed, after the “technical issue” forced the airport to suspend arrivals.
But it warned that “disruption is expected to continue”, asking passengers in an X post to check with their airline before travelling to the airport.
The air traffic chaos follow a technical glitch in July last year that saw scores of flights to and from the UK cancelled, prompting anger from airline chiefs.
Britain meanwhile suffered its worst air systems failure in years in 2023, with more than 700,000 passengers affected after hundreds of flights were delayed or cancelled.
Responding to the latest fallout, NATS said: “We know this is hugely frustrating and apologise unreservedly.”
‘Absolute nightmare’
Caught up by the glitch, healthcare worker Josie Donoghue said it had been “an absolute nightmare” at London’s Gatwick airport, having had to disembark her flight to Ireland after three hours stuck on the runway.
“Getting through that airport was like trying to get out of Alcatraz,” she told Britain’s domestic Press Association news agency.
Liverpool, Birmingham and Edinburgh airports were also affected, while Dublin airport said it had cancelled dozens of flights.
Ryanair said more than 65,000 of its passengers had been disrupted and it had cancelled more than 50 flights.
English football club Arsenal, due to play Napoli in the Champions League Wednesday in the southern Italian city, was forced to cancel a news conference after the team’s flight was delayed. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Washington slams Chinese AI firms for ‘systematic’ theft of US model capabilities
deduped_items.summary: WASHINGTON, Sept 9 — Washington accused top Chinese artificial intelligence labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot A...
deduped_items.body_text:
WASHINGTON, Sept 9 — Washington accused top Chinese artificial intelligence labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI of systematically stealing the capabilities of American models today as the two countries race for tech supremacy.
The advisory from the US cyber defence agency comes ahead of an expected meeting this month between President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping at the White House, where AI could be an important discussion topic.
It follows several previous accusations of Chinese AI theft through a process known as distillation, levelled by the US government and American AI companies.
“China-based artificial intelligence (AI) companies are conducting systematic extraction of proprietary functionalities and capabilities of US AI companies’ models,” yesterday’s advisory read.
They are doing so “through industrial-scale knowledge distillation campaigns that form the core — not merely a supplement — of their AI development strategy”, it said.
Distillation is where an AI model is trained to mimic the output of a larger, more capable one.
The method is widely used across the industry, but Washington says Chinese firms have deployed it at scale to illicitly copy American systems.
Chinese companies that adopt this strategy “see significantly shorter AI development timelines and reduced financial expenditures in training a frontier model”, the advisory said.
It detailed how DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI allegedly used millions of exchanges and requests to steal the capabilities of US models from the likes of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI.
These actions, taken “likely with Chinese government awareness”, have taken place since at least late 2024, it said.
AFP contacted the Chinese companies apart from StepFun which was not immediately reachable. Moonshot AI declined to comment.
Trump is under pressure to respond to the increasing success of Chinese AI models that many companies prefer to the more powerful, but pricier, US versions from Anthropic or OpenAI.
In July, dozens of startups wrote a letter to the Trump administration urging it to think twice against any outright ban or strict curbs on foreign-made AI models, saying this should only be considered for government use of the technology.
That month, Beijing also turned the tables by accusing US AI of using Chinese examples to train their models.
Asked about the accusations at a regular briefing today, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she had not seen the specific US report but the country should “refrain from making unfounded accusations against and smearing China”.
“The development of artificial intelligence in China is the result of achieving high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology,” she said.
“Both China and the United States are major countries in the field of AI. We should strengthen cooperation.” — AFP

The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said analysis of Himawari-9 satellite imagery at 7am detected volcanic ash from Mount Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara and Mount Dukono and Mount Ibu in North Maluku, alongside ash from Anak Krakatau in the Sunda Strait.
Of the four volcanoes, BMKG said ash from Ili Lewotolok, located on Lembata Island in East Nusa Tenggara in eastern Indonesia, was observed at the highest altitude of up to 8,000 feet (about 2,438 metres), moving northwest to north across parts of Lembata Regency and the Flores Strait.
“The public is urged not to panic, but to remain vigilant, continue monitoring information on volcanic ash distribution and refer to verified information from official sources,” the agency said in its latest post on social media.
Volcanic ash from Ili Lewotolok forced Wunopito Airport in Lewoleba to temporarily close on Tuesday, with the closure subsequently extended until an estimated 7am local time on Thursday, according to state-owned air navigation service provider AirNav Indonesia.
Meanwhile, all eight airports that have been temporarily closed since Sunday due to volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau had reopened by Tuesday, including Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Indonesia’s main international gateway.
Separately, Lampung’s Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD) said a monitoring operation at 10am by the Indonesian Navy vessel KRI Lepu-861 found that eruptive activity at Anak Krakatau remained observable, marked by smoke and volcanic ash.
The agency said the monitoring, which also drew on Himawari-9 satellite imagery, detected ash reaching up to 7,000 feet (about 2,134 metres) and moving northwest, covering part of Lampung Bay. — Bernama

deduped_items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 9 — Volcanic ash from three more Indonesian volcanoes was reported across parts of the archipelago o...
deduped_items.body_text:
JAKARTA, Sept 9 — Volcanic ash from three more Indonesian volcanoes was reported across parts of the archipelago on Wednesday, in addition to Mount Anak Krakatau, with ash from one of them continuing to disrupt air travel in East Nusa Tenggara.
The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said analysis of Himawari-9 satellite imagery at 7am detected volcanic ash from Mount Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara and Mount Dukono and Mount Ibu in North Maluku, alongside ash from Anak Krakatau in the Sunda Strait.
Of the four volcanoes, BMKG said ash from Ili Lewotolok, located on Lembata Island in East Nusa Tenggara in eastern Indonesia, was observed at the highest altitude of up to 8,000 feet (about 2,438 metres), moving northwest to north across parts of Lembata Regency and the Flores Strait.
“The public is urged not to panic, but to remain vigilant, continue monitoring information on volcanic ash distribution and refer to verified information from official sources,” the agency said in its latest post on social media.
Volcanic ash from Ili Lewotolok forced Wunopito Airport in Lewoleba to temporarily close on Tuesday, with the closure subsequently extended until an estimated 7am local time on Thursday, according to state-owned air navigation service provider AirNav Indonesia.
Meanwhile, all eight airports that have been temporarily closed since Sunday due to volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau had reopened by Tuesday, including Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, Indonesia’s main international gateway.
Separately, Lampung’s Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD) said a monitoring operation at 10am by the Indonesian Navy vessel KRI Lepu-861 found that eruptive activity at Anak Krakatau remained observable, marked by smoke and volcanic ash.
The agency said the monitoring, which also drew on Himawari-9 satellite imagery, detected ash reaching up to 7,000 feet (about 2,134 metres) and moving northwest, covering part of Lampung Bay. — Bernama
