deduped_items.body_text:
•Dr Tunji Alausa, Minister of Education
…Plans digital tracking of lecturers, equipment, facilities
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja
ABUJA — The Federal Government has moved to overhaul the accreditation system for Nigerian universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, warning institutions against presenting a false or temporary picture of their academic and infrastructural capacity during accreditation exercises.
The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, gave the warning in Abuja on Tuesday while inaugurating a Ministerial Committee on Strengthening the Accreditation and Quality Assurance System for Tertiary Institutions in Nigeria.
Alausa said the era of temporarily assembling lecturers, equipment and facilities ahead of accreditation visits must end, stressing that institutions should be assessed on resources that are genuinely available and sustainable.
He said the government would deploy digital technology, identity-management systems, geospatial mapping and other verification mechanisms to ensure that what institutions present to accreditation teams reflects their actual capacity.
“An institution should not be able to prepare a temporary picture of itself simply for the purpose of an accreditation visit. Sadly, this is what we see in a majority of instances,” the minister said.
Alausa expressed concern over the temporary movement of academic and non-academic personnel between institutions, as well as the borrowing or relocation of laboratory equipment, workshop resources, library materials and other facilities solely to impress accreditation teams.
He said such practices undermined the integrity of the tertiary education system and denied students access to the resources and personnel used to secure approval for academic programmes.
“We must ensure that when an accreditation team visits an institution, what it sees and verifies should represent the actual and sustainable capacity of that institution, not an arrangement assembled for the accreditation exercise,” he said.
Digital tracking of facilities, equipment
To close the loopholes, Alausa directed the National Universities Commission, NUC; National Board for Technical Education, NBTE; and National Commission for Colleges of Education, NCCE, to progressively move away from predominantly manual and episodic accreditation procedures to a digital, data-driven and continuously verifiable system.
He said geospatial mapping, geotagging and digital identification technologies should be considered for physical infrastructure, laboratories, workshops and major equipment presented during accreditation.
Under the proposed system, critical equipment used to secure accreditation would have unique digital records linked to the institution and its physical location, making it difficult for institutions to borrow or move resources merely to pass accreditation.
The minister said the same principle should apply to lecturers and other personnel.
He called for a comprehensive digital identity-management and staff-verification framework capable of establishing that individuals presented as employees of an institution were genuinely affiliated with it.
Alausa said the government would explore collaboration with the National Identity Management Commission, NIMC, including the use of the National Identification Number, NIN, alongside other appropriate and secure technologies.
“The objective is straightforward: one individual, one verifiable identity and an accurately declared institutional affiliation,” he said.
He added that the system should be capable of detecting cases where an individual was improperly presented as full-time personnel in more than one institution.
The minister also said the proposed reforms would ensure that the actual composition of academic departments, including junior academic staff and other personnel who genuinely constitute the workforce, was captured digitally.
According to him, this would prevent accreditation decisions from being based on inflated or manipulat

deduped_items.title: More champagne for a few, no water for All: SA’s water tanker disaster
deduped_items.summary: South Africa’s water crisis is no longer just about dry taps, but what happens when emergency measures become a permanent business model. As municipalities spend hundreds of millions on water tankers, people remain trapped without reliable infrastructure. The question is no longer whether tankers are necessary, but who benefits when the emergency never ends and how long South Africans can afford to pay for failure.

deduped_items.title: Election interference activities revealed
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Election interference activities revealedBALLOT INTEGRITY: Groups engaging in activities such as unlicensed money lending and election betting often serve Beijing’s vote disruption efforts, authorities said
  - By Lu Yun-feng, Jonathan Chin and Sam Garcia / Staff reporter, with staff writers and CNA
 The authorities have launched 54 probes into suspected foreign election interference and other electoral fraud-related crimes to protect the integrity of the Nov. 28 local elections, the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau said yesterday. Special agents launched investigations into illegal foreign campaign contributions, money laundering and election betting ahead of the “nine-in-one” elections, the bureau said. The investigations resulted in 25 pretrial detentions, 70 suspects placed on bail, and the confiscation of NT$62.8 billion (US$2 billion) linked to suspected illegal cash flows used in breaking election laws, it said. Huang Wen-yang, head of the Ministry of Justice Investigation Bureau’s Criminal Investigation Division, speaks at a press conference in New Taipei City yesterday, saying authorities had uncovered 54 cases involving more than NT$62.8 billion in illicit funds.Photo: CNA The bureau interviewed 559 people as potential suspects or witnesses, it added. The investigations were part of the law enforcement effort to prevent foreign election interference, it said, adding that it is focusing on unlicensed money lending, election betting, and money launderers operating under shell corporations and virtual buyer groups. Organizations and groups engaging in such activities often serve as conduits for funds used in election interference by Beijing, it said. Another goal of the operation is to identify those who benefited from the Chinese government’s illegal campaign contributions, it said. The bureau said it assigned 25 field offices to the effort, seizing NT$11.19 billion from unregistered moneylenders, NT$4.24 billion from alleged launderers and N$5.06 billion from alleged tax evaders. The seizures included NT$153 million in cash, 521 bank accounts holding a total of NT$501 million, Tether cryptocurrency valued at US$2,184, 12 luxury cars valued at NT$23 million, luxury fashion accessories valued at NT$9.1 million, watches valued at NT$10 million and 35 properties valued at NT$101 million, the bureau said. The properties and assets were deemed proceeds from suspected criminal activities, it said. The bureau warned political candidates and members of the public against receiving or facilitating the transfer of suspicious funds from China or other countries. Protecting elections’ integrity is a national security matter, and money laundering prevention is necessary to ensure the orderly functioning of the financial market, it added. Separately yesterday, the High Prosecutors’ Office said that prosecutors uncovered 212 cases of illicit financial transactions intended to influence the elections, seizing more than NT$900 million in suspected criminal proceeds. The office launched a crackdown on illicit financial flows nationwide from Aug. 17 to Friday last week to prevent illicit funds from influencing the elections, prosecutors said in a news release. The operation uncovered 212 cases involving illicit financial flows and 588 people suspected of breaching the Banking Act (銀行法), the Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法) and gambling provisions of the Criminal Code, they said. Prosecutors detained 75 people, while 229 were released on bail, and the remainder were subject to other measures, including residence restrictions, it added. Authorities seized about NT$909 million in suspected criminal proceeds in cash and bank accounts, as well as more than 390,000 Tether tokens, 20 vehicles and 850 electronic devices, such as mobile phones, tablets and computers, the office said. They also seized 36 properties and more than 100 luxury items, including designer bags, watches and gold jewelry, it added.

deduped_items.title: Japan delegations urge closer Taiwan cooperation
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Japan delegations urge closer Taiwan cooperation
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 A senior member of the Japan Innovation Party (JIP) yesterday called for closer Tokyo-Taipei cooperation, including on drone and space-based technologies, to meet modern defense needs and promote regional peace and stability. Nobuyuki Baba, former JIP leader and head of the party’s Japan-Republic of China Friendship Study Group, met earlier yesterday with President William Lai (賴清德) at the Presidential Office in Taipei, and discussed bilateral relations, US-China ties and other issues. Speaking at a press briefing, Baba thanked Taiwan for its generous donations to help people affected by a magnitude 7.1 earthquake that struck Japan’s Kumamoto Prefecture late last month, causing widespread infrastructure damage and transportation disruptions and killing at least 38 people. Nobuyuki Baba, left, head of the Japan Innovation Party’s Japan-Republic of China Friendship Study Group, clinks mugs with President William Lai at the Presidential Office in Taipei yesterday.Photo: Screen grab from the Presidential Office’s Flickr page “True friendship reveals itself through adversity,” he said, adding that Japan and Taiwan have always been there for each other in times of crisis. The Taiwanese government said that a dedicated bank account set up to accept private donations for the quake had reached more than NT$300 million (US$9.51 million). The government also donated NT$5 million to support reconstruction efforts in Kumamoto, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said. Baba said his delegation and Lai agreed that both sides should continue to deepen bilateral cooperation and exchanges in areas such as the economy, culture, tourism and natural disaster preparedness. On regional security, Baba said that Lai told him that Taiwan is strengthening its self-defense capabilities. The Japanese government is also considering strengthening its self-defense capabilities amid rising regional and global tensions, he said. The JIP, the junior coalition partner of Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), also hopes to harness drone and space-based technologies to revolutionize national defense and logistics and meet the challenges posed by modern warfare, Baba said. Tokyo and Taipei should work together to complement each other’s capabilities and jointly develop cutting-edge technologies, including drones, he said. At the meeting, Lai told the JIP delegation that Taiwan looks forward to an even stronger partnership between the two countries under the LDP-JIP coalition, to jointly build a “non-red” supply chain, thereby enhancing the resilience of global democratic supply chains and strengthening economic and trade cooperation, Lai said. Separately yesterday, a delegation from the Japanese cross-party parliamentary group “Diet Members’ Association for Peace and Stability in the Taiwan Strait” arrived in Taipei for a three-day visit. The delegation is led by Haruo Kitamura, a member of the House of Councilors from the Conservative Party of Japan. Kitamura said Taiwan is Japan’s most important friend, adding that peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait are important not only to Taiwan, but also “vital to Japan’s very survival.” He specifically cited two legislative goals, pointing to the US’ Taiwan Relations Act and Taiwan Travel Act. He said Japan must, “by all means,” pass its own versions of the two laws to allow Japan to work with the US to continue conveying to the world the close ties between Japan and Taiwan and their peoples. “Only by doing so can we take the most critical step toward safeguarding peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait,” he said. Additional reporting by Fang Wei-li

deduped_items.title: Medical visits top 110,000 as flu epidemic spreads
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Medical visits top 110,000 as flu epidemic spreads
  - By Lee I-chia / Staff reporter
 The seasonal flu has entered an epidemic period, with more than 110,000 medical visits, 19 deaths and 105 severe cases reported last week, the Centers for Disease Control (CDC) said yesterday. The centers also reported the youngest severe COVID-19 case on record in Taiwan and two new cases of acute hepatitis C linked to a cluster in New Taipei City. Influenza and COVID-19 viruses were the most common respiratory pathogen spreading locally in the past four weeks, CDC Epidemic Intelligence Center Director Guo Hung-wei (郭宏偉) said, adding that influenza A(H1N1) was the dominant flu strain detected. Centers for Disease Control Epidemic Intelligence Center Director Guo Hung-wei speaks at a news conference in Taipei yesterday.Photo: CNA There were 115,136 medical visits for flu-like illnesses from Aug. 30 to Saturday last week, 11.2 percent of which were emergency cases, surpassing the epidemic threshold of 11 percent, he said. “We have entered the flu epidemic period,” he said. A total of 105 severe flu cases and 19 flu-related deaths were confirmed between Tuesday last week and Monday, and more than 80 percent of them have or had chronic underlying conditions, he said. As for COVID-19, there were 20,199 medical visits from Aug. 30 to Saturday last week, slightly lower than the week before, but still at a relatively high level, he said, adding that 73 severe cases and 15 deaths were confirmed between Tuesday last week and Monday. Among the severe COVID-19 cases was a less than month-old baby who does not have underlying health conditions, and is not eligible for vaccination, making it the youngest severe case on record, CDC physician Lin Yung-ching (林詠青) said. The boy had a mild fever and nose congestion late last month and was taken to see a doctor the next day, but as his symptoms persisted, he was hospitalized this month and later transferred to an intensive care unit when he experienced difficulty breathing and respiratory distress, and was confirmed to have pneumonia, he said. Contact tracing found that the boy had been exposed to a person who has COVID-19, Lin added. CDC Deputy Director-General Lin Min-cheng (林明誠) said that medical visits for flu-like illness last week was the highest of the same week in a decade, and is expected to continue increasing in the next four weeks. While COVID-19 cases have dropped, severe cases and the number of deaths remain high, he added. The CDC also provided an update on a cluster of confirmed acute viral hepatitis C cases traced to a clinic in New Taipei City, with two more cases identified through expanded testing, Lin Min-cheng said. The CDC last week reported 11 confirmed cases who all received injections at the Antai Songhe Clinic (安泰淞鶴診所). With the onset of symptoms occurring between Jan. 29 and Aug. 18, 1,118 people who received an injection at the clinic between July 1 last year and Aug. 27 are urged to get a blood test, it said. As of Monday, 1,096 people have been notified and 353 have ben tested, Lin Min-cheng said. Two were confirmed to have acute viral hepatitis C — a woman in her 60s who is asymptomatic and a man in his 50s who has symptoms including loss of appetite, dark urine and general fatigue, and has been hospitalized for treatment, he said. Experts had estimated that the positivity rate would be about 5 percent, but so far only two had been confirmed among the 353 tested, which is an encouraging sign, he said, adding that testing and follow-ups were ongoing. Symptoms of acute viral hepatitis C may vary, so the absence of symptoms does not necessarily mean no infection, he said, urging those who have been notified to get tested as soon as possible.

deduped_items.summary: Digital bank ZA Bank is taking 45,000 square feet (4,181 square metres) across four upper floors at Hysan Development’s Lee Garden Eight for its new headquarters, adding to a wave of financial and technology companies reshaping Causeway Bay’s commercial landscape. The move comes as landlords across the district grapple with a changing property market marked by excess office space. The bank is scheduled to move into Tower 3 in 2027, coinciding with Hysan and partner Chinachem Group completing the
deduped_items.body_text:
Hysan courts fintech office portfolio as ZA Bank commits to new Causeway Bay headquarters
As landlords navigate soft office demand, tech and digital enterprises are stepping in to capitalise on falling rents and more favourable terms
Digital bank ZA Bank is taking 45,000 square feet (4,181 square metres) across four upper floors at Hysan Development’s Lee Garden Eight for its new headquarters, adding to a wave of financial and technology companies reshaping Causeway Bay’s commercial landscape.
The leasing push comes as Causeway Bay and Wan Chai continue to absorb office supply, with demand recovering more slowly than in Central. Grade A office vacancy in the two districts stood at 9.8 per cent in August, according to property consultancy JLL.
Hysan’s office portfolio was 93 per cent occupied at the end of June, down from 94 per cent six months earlier. Office turnover fell 1.3 per cent in the first half to HK$694 million (US$88.5 million), while rental reversions remained negative, according to interim results published in August.
“The new economy tenant portfolio is becoming stronger,” said Ricky Lui, Hysan’s executive director and chief operating officer. Leasing activity, he noted, had picked up recently, with the current tenant mix roughly split among financial services, professional services and co-working operators.

deduped_items.summary: China has accused Philippine officials of “grandstanding and lying” after Manila’s defence secretary publicly read aloud a Chinese diplomat’s note on the South China Sea that the Philippine minister described as “coercion, bullying and aggression”. “We urge certain people in the Philippines to stop this grandstanding and lying, and to protect China-Philippine relations and the peace and stability in the South China Sea,” Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said. Mao was responding to..
deduped_items.body_text:
Beijing tells Manila to ‘stop lying’ after minister exposes South China Sea note
At Seoul Defence Dialogue, Gilberto Teodoro Jnr brands China’s handwritten memo on arbitration ruling as ‘coercion and bullying’
“We urge certain people in the Philippines to stop this grandstanding and lying, and to protect China-Philippine relations and the peace and stability in the South China Sea,” Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said.
Teodoro read out parts of the handwritten note, which included Beijing’s rejection of the arbitration and a statement that the award in 2016 denying most of China’s claims in the South China Sea, was “illegal, null and void”.
The forum organiser later said the note came from a military attache at the Chinese embassy in Seoul, who passed it to a forum staff member and asked that it be given to Teodoro, according to South Korean news agency Yonhap.
Teodoro said the move was impolite to their South Korean hosts.

deduped_items.title: Hysan courts fintech office portfolio as ZA Bank commits to new Causeway Bay headquarters
deduped_items.summary: Digital bank ZA Bank is taking 45,000 square feet (4,181 square metres) across four upper floors at Hysan Development’s Lee Garden Eight for its new headquarters, adding to a wave of financial and technology companies reshaping Causeway Bay’s commercial landscape. The move comes as landlords across the district grapple with a changing property market marked by excess office space. The bank is scheduled to move into Tower 3 in 2027, coinciding with Hysan and partner Chinachem Group completing the
deduped_items.body_text:
Hysan courts fintech office portfolio as ZA Bank commits to new Causeway Bay headquarters
As landlords navigate soft office demand, tech and digital enterprises are stepping in to capitalise on falling rents and more favourable terms
Digital bank ZA Bank is taking 45,000 square feet (4,181 square metres) across four upper floors at Hysan Development’s Lee Garden Eight for its new headquarters, adding to a wave of financial and technology companies reshaping Causeway Bay’s commercial landscape.
The leasing push comes as Causeway Bay and Wan Chai continue to absorb office supply, with demand recovering more slowly than in Central. Grade A office vacancy in the two districts stood at 9.8 per cent in August, according to property consultancy JLL.
Hysan’s office portfolio was 93 per cent occupied at the end of June, down from 94 per cent six months earlier. Office turnover fell 1.3 per cent in the first half to HK$694 million (US$88.5 million), while rental reversions remained negative, according to interim results published in August.
“The new economy tenant portfolio is becoming stronger,” said Ricky Lui, Hysan’s executive director and chief operating officer. Leasing activity, he noted, had picked up recently, with the current tenant mix roughly split among financial services, professional services and co-working operators.

deduped_items.summary: 蘋果2026秋季發表會將於9月10日凌晨1點，在美國加州Apple Park總部的Steve Jobs Theater登場。就在發表會前夕，蘋果先舉辦一場私人晚宴，現場眾星雲集，沒想到五月天阿信也驚喜現身，還直接在Facebook等個人社群平台打卡，立刻讓大批粉絲暴動，紛紛敲碗「期待開箱」。 今（9日）傍晚，阿信在社群上傳照片，只見晚宴長桌上擺著寫有「mayday ashin」的名牌，後方則能看到彩虹造型拱門。阿信還引用五月天〈知足〉歌詞寫下：「怎麼去擁有一道彩虹？」瞬間勾起不少粉絲回憶。 從其他賓客分享的照片也能看到，阿信當晚穿著一身黑色西裝，整體造型相當有型，胸前還…

deduped_items.summary: 蘋果2026秋季發表會將於9月10日凌晨1點，在美國加州Apple Park總部的Steve Jobs Theater登場。就在發表會前夕，蘋果先舉辦一場私人晚宴，現場眾星雲集，沒想到五月天阿信也驚喜現身，還直接在Facebook等個人社群平台打卡，立刻讓大批粉絲暴動，紛紛敲碗「期待開箱」。 今（9日）傍晚，阿信在社群上傳照片，只見晚宴長桌上擺著寫有「mayday ashin」的名牌，後方則能看到彩虹造型拱門。阿信還引用五月天〈知足〉歌詞寫下：「怎麼去擁有一道彩虹？」瞬間勾起不少粉絲回憶。 從其他賓客分享的照片也能看到，阿信當晚穿著一身黑色西裝，整體造型相當有型，胸前還…

deduped_items.body_text:
South Korea’s military pushed back against claims that its troops have increasingly overlooked North Korean soldiers crossing the inter-Korean border, denying that commanders have eased their response to incursions along the Military Demarcation Line (MDL).
“Our military is taking firm operational measures against North Korean violations of the MDL in accordance with established standards and principles,” the ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said in a statement provided to NK News on Wednesday.

deduped_items.title: ‘Costly lemon’ or life-changing laws? Victoria to become first in Australia to offer right to work from home
deduped_items.summary: The Carroll government has made several amendments to the bill after consulting with business leaders. How will the laws work, and will they last?Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastAustralian-first laws that would guarantee workers the right to work from home two days a week are expected to pass the Victorian parliament this week.The laws were first announced in 2025 by the then premier, Jacinta Allan, just months after Peter Dutton and the Coalition lost the federal elec
deduped_items.body_text:
Australian-first laws that would guarantee workers the right to work from home two days a week are expected to pass the Victorian parliament this week.
Despite widespread opposition to the proposal from some of the country’s largest business lobby groups, the equal opportunity amendment (work from home) bill passed parliament’s lower house – with support from the Coalition – in July.
That same week, Ben Carroll toppled Allan as Labor leader. One of his first moves as premier was to pause debate in the upper house to allow for consultation with business leaders – and on Wednesday, the government confirmed several amendments to the bill following these discussions.
Here’s what we know.

deduped_items.title: Pour émuler Vivaldi au rythme des saisons
deduped_items.summary: «Les quatre saisons du Québec», de François Dompierre, est la seconde collaboration entre le compositeur et Francis Choinière
deduped_items.body_text:
Le vendredi 11 septembre, Francis Choinière, son Orchestre FILMharmonique et la violoniste Isabella d’Éloize Perron présenteront aux Montréalais en grande première Les quatre saisons du Québec de François Dompierre. Entretien avec le chef avant cette création.
Présenté comme une « première mondiale », le concert du 11 septembre à la Maison symphonique sera en fait une « quatrième », puisque les artistes ont déjà proposé ce même programme — associant Les quatre saisons de Vivaldi, Les quatre saisons de Buenos Aires d’Astor Piazzolla et Les quatre saisons du Québec de François Dompierre — au Palais Montcalm de Québec vendredi et samedi derniers et à la salle Les-frères-Lemaire de Victoriaville dimanche.
Encouragement
Le disque et les fichiers permettant de découvrir l’œuvre en téléchargement ou en écoute à la demande sont même accessibles depuis le 28 août. « C’est ce que l’on veut faire désormais. Pour l’enregistrement en général, mais tout particulièrement pour de nouvelles créations. Je crois que c’est encore plus important que les gens puissent découvrir une œuvre avant d’entrer en salle. Ça permet une meilleure appréciation, une meilleure capacité d’écoute et de compréhension de l’œuvre », dit au Devoir le chef Francis Choinière, désormais partie prenante dans les décisions artistiques de l’étiquette Atma, qui a publié l’enregistrement.
« Même dans l’industrie du film, très souvent la trame sonore va être disponible avant le film. Idem pour une nouvelle création de Broadway : les promoteurs veulent exposer quelque peu les gens à la musique avant qu’ils l’entendent en spectacle. »
Le projet des Quatre saisons du Québec est né dans la foulée de la création du Requiem. « Avant tout ça, François Dompierre avait plutôt déclaré que ça ne lui tentait plus vraiment de composer. Mais après le Requiem, je me souviens, en coulisses, juste avant de monter sur scène, il m’avait dit : “Si jamais tu as d’autres trips comme ça, moi je suis partant.” Donc, deux ou trois mois plus tard, je lui ai fait une proposition : “Nous avons notre tournée des Quatre saisons. Ça fait trois ou quatre fois qu’on fait cette tournée-là et on aimerait la renouveler avec une nouvelle œuvre. Est-ce que ça te tenterait de composer Les quatre saisons du Québec ?” Il y a réfléchi une ou deux semaines et a dit oui. Il a composé l’œuvre en trois ou quatre mois et on l’a enregistrée deux mois plus tard, en mars 2026, pour une sortie avant la tournée. »
Avec l’ancienne mouture à huit saisons (Vivaldi et Piazzolla), Francis Choinière, l’Orchestre FILMharmonique et Isabella d’Éloize Perron s’étaient rendus aux États-Unis, notamment à Carnegie Hall. Avec la création et les douze saisons, ce sera bientôt l’Europe : Paris, Bordeaux, Vienne, Berlin et Prague.
Profondément québécois
Dans sa très habile et attachante composition, qui s’articule comme un « concerto symphonique en quatre mouvements » (allegro/rigaudon ; mouvement lent/complainte ; scherzo/valse, contredanse ; Finale/quadrille), François Dompierre procède un peu comme Astor Piazzolla. Si le tango de Piazzolla est indissociable de l’Argentine (l’agencement en « Quatre saisons » étant, lui, dû au compositeur russe Leonid Desyatnikov à l’instigation de Gidon Kremer), les thèmes de Dompierre sont profondément québécois, ce qui fait la réussite du projet.
« En fait, chaque mouvement contient un petit clin d’œil à Vivaldi, note le chef d’orchestre. Il y en a qui sont plus évidents que d’autres. Mais je crois que l’approche était un peu plus dans le style folklore et le style violoneux pour les solos. C’était l’approche que nous voulions : quelque chose de québécois. Ce sont les inspirations, les idées de François Dompierre. Je l’ai juste guidé au sens où je voulais quelques rappels de Vivaldi pour arrimer le programme. »
Ces projets avec l’Orchestre FILMharmonique et Francis Choinière ont remis le pied à l’étrier à François Dompierre. « Il va écrire plus d’œuvres. Je ne veux pas me prononcer, parce que ce n’est pas c

deduped_items.body_text:
Le vendredi 11 septembre, Francis Choinière, son Orchestre FILMharmonique et la violoniste Isabella d’Éloize Perron présenteront aux Montréalais en grande première Les quatre saisons du Québec de François Dompierre. Entretien avec le chef avant cette création.
Présenté comme une « première mondiale », le concert du 11 septembre à la Maison symphonique sera en fait une « quatrième », puisque les artistes ont déjà proposé ce même programme — associant Les quatre saisons de Vivaldi, Les quatre saisons de Buenos Aires d’Astor Piazzolla et Les quatre saisons du Québec de François Dompierre — au Palais Montcalm de Québec vendredi et samedi derniers et à la salle Les-frères-Lemaire de Victoriaville dimanche.
Encouragement
Le disque et les fichiers permettant de découvrir l’œuvre en téléchargement ou en écoute à la demande sont même accessibles depuis le 28 août. « C’est ce que l’on veut faire désormais. Pour l’enregistrement en général, mais tout particulièrement pour de nouvelles créations. Je crois que c’est encore plus important que les gens puissent découvrir une œuvre avant d’entrer en salle. Ça permet une meilleure appréciation, une meilleure capacité d’écoute et de compréhension de l’œuvre », dit au Devoir le chef Francis Choinière, désormais partie prenante dans les décisions artistiques de l’étiquette Atma, qui a publié l’enregistrement.
« Même dans l’industrie du film, très souvent la trame sonore va être disponible avant le film. Idem pour une nouvelle création de Broadway : les promoteurs veulent exposer quelque peu les gens à la musique avant qu’ils l’entendent en spectacle. »
Le projet des Quatre saisons du Québec est né dans la foulée de la création du Requiem. « Avant tout ça, François Dompierre avait plutôt déclaré que ça ne lui tentait plus vraiment de composer. Mais après le Requiem, je me souviens, en coulisses, juste avant de monter sur scène, il m’avait dit : “Si jamais tu as d’autres trips comme ça, moi je suis partant.” Donc, deux ou trois mois plus tard, je lui ai fait une proposition : “Nous avons notre tournée des Quatre saisons. Ça fait trois ou quatre fois qu’on fait cette tournée-là et on aimerait la renouveler avec une nouvelle œuvre. Est-ce que ça te tenterait de composer Les quatre saisons du Québec ?” Il y a réfléchi une ou deux semaines et a dit oui. Il a composé l’œuvre en trois ou quatre mois et on l’a enregistrée deux mois plus tard, en mars 2026, pour une sortie avant la tournée. »
Avec l’ancienne mouture à huit saisons (Vivaldi et Piazzolla), Francis Choinière, l’Orchestre FILMharmonique et Isabella d’Éloize Perron s’étaient rendus aux États-Unis, notamment à Carnegie Hall. Avec la création et les douze saisons, ce sera bientôt l’Europe : Paris, Bordeaux, Vienne, Berlin et Prague.
Profondément québécois
Dans sa très habile et attachante composition, qui s’articule comme un « concerto symphonique en quatre mouvements » (allegro/rigaudon ; mouvement lent/complainte ; scherzo/valse, contredanse ; Finale/quadrille), François Dompierre procède un peu comme Astor Piazzolla. Si le tango de Piazzolla est indissociable de l’Argentine (l’agencement en « Quatre saisons » étant, lui, dû au compositeur russe Leonid Desyatnikov à l’instigation de Gidon Kremer), les thèmes de Dompierre sont profondément québécois, ce qui fait la réussite du projet.
« En fait, chaque mouvement contient un petit clin d’œil à Vivaldi, note le chef d’orchestre. Il y en a qui sont plus évidents que d’autres. Mais je crois que l’approche était un peu plus dans le style folklore et le style violoneux pour les solos. C’était l’approche que nous voulions : quelque chose de québécois. Ce sont les inspirations, les idées de François Dompierre. Je l’ai juste guidé au sens où je voulais quelques rappels de Vivaldi pour arrimer le programme. »

deduped_items.body_text:
spaña, Francia, Reino Unido, Canadá, Dinamarca, Finlandia, Irlanda, Islandia, Noruega, Polonia, Portugal y Suecia sancionarán el comercio de bienes con asentamientos ilegales de Israel en Cisjordania reocupada en protesta por la violencia de los colonos contra los palestinos y la expansión de esas comunidades. Los ministros de Relaciones Exteriores de los 12 países publicaron una declaración conjunta, en la cual denuncian que “las acciones del gobierno de Israel en Cisjordania están socavando la posibilidad de una solución de dos estados”, en referencia a un plan según el cual dos estados –uno israelí y otro palestino– vivirían pacíficamente uno al lado del otro, y advierten sobre un rápido deterioro de la situación “en un contexto de niveles sin precedentes de violencia de colonos y expansión de los asentamientos”. Según la legislación internacional, todas las colonias o asentamientos israelíes en Cisjordania, territorio ocupado desde 1967, son ilegales.
El primer ministro israelí y prófugo de la Corte Penal Internacional, Benjamin Netanyahu, ha prometido continuar con la expansión de los asentamientos en Cisjordania pese a la creciente presión internacional. El ministro de Exteriores, Gideon Saar, consideró la decisión una “interferencia inaceptable en el proceso electoral de un Estado soberano” y amenazó con que “el mensaje para cualquier gobierno que nos dañe es claro: Israel actuará contra él y perderán su influencia y relevancia en la región”. Por ahora, ordenó el cierre del consulado británico en Jerusalén Este –representación del Reino Unido ante la Autoridad Nacional Palestina (ANP)–, expulsó a ese país del Centro de Coordinación Civil y Militar multinacional (órgano patrocinado por Washington para supervisar el supuesto alto el fuego en Gaza), prohibió entrenar a las fuerzas de seguridad de la ANP e impidió la entrada a 12 ciudadanos británicos, incluido el ex líder laborista Jeremy Corbyn.
La reacción destemplada del régimen sionista contrasta con la suavidad de las sanciones: apenas 5 por ciento de sus exportaciones procede de los asentamientos ilegales, y es evidente que no toda esa producción tiene como destino los países que han tomado acciones contra la ocupación. Más que la severidad de las restricciones comerciales, la ira de Tel Aviv refleja la completa impunidad que la comunidad internacional le ha dispensado mientras perpetra contra el pueblo palestino uno de los peores crímenes de la historia. Las sanciones llegan sólo cuando los colonos ilegales han convertido las masacres de palestinos del pasatiempo ocasional que ha sido por décadas en una tarea de tiempo completo, siempre bajo la mirada y protección de las fuerzas armadas israelíes. Cuando el primer ministro y los miembros de su gabinete declaran sin tapujos que su intención es exterminar a los palestinos y que ni siquiera los consideran seres humanos. Cuando la totalidad de Cisjordania se encuentra bajo control israelí y los ocupantes mantienen secuestrados dentro de su propia tierra a 3 millones de personas.
Como señaló la relatora especial de la Organización de Naciones Unidas (ONU) para los Territorios Palestinos Ocupados, Francesca Albanese, la prohibición comercial contra los asentamientos israelíes ilegales es un comienzo muy necesario, pero sólo eso: un punto de partida. Para poner fin a la complicidad con el genocidio, es preciso un cerco financiero completo a Israel, la prohibición absoluta de la compra o venta de armas, acabar con toda forma de colaboración con las autoridades israelíes y la ejecución de las órdenes de captura que pesan sobre los criminales de guerra, así como la conformación de un fondo internacional para la reconstrucción de Gaza y el regreso seguro de todos los palestinos desplazados desde 1948.

deduped_items.title: Las presiones fiscales en las tasas de interés
deduped_items.summary: Desde finales de 2021, las tasas de interés de largo plazo de los bonos gubernamentales de la mayoría de las economías avanzadas han mostrado trayectorias ascendentes hasta alcanzar, en algunos casos, niveles no observados desde antes de la gran crisis financiera global de 2007-2008.
deduped_items.body_text:
Desde finales de 2021, las tasas de interés de largo plazo de los bonos gubernamentales de la mayoría de las economías avanzadas han mostrado trayectorias ascendentes hasta alcanzar, en algunos casos, niveles no observados desde antes de la gran crisis financiera global de 2007-2008.
El alza ha sido especialmente marcada en los rendimientos de la deuda soberana a treinta años. Por ejemplo, de diciembre de 2021 a agosto de 2026, la rentabilidad del bono del Tesoro de Estados Unidos aumentó 317 puntos base, para ubicarse en 5.25 por ciento, el mayor nivel desde junio de 2007. Los incrementos de las tasas en el Reino Unido, Francia, Alemania y Japón fueron mayores, aunque, con excepción del primero, los niveles se mantuvieron por debajo de los de Estados Unidos.
Durante el mismo periodo, los rendimientos de los bonos de diez años de esos países registraron aumentos similares a los de treinta años, alcanzando niveles elevados desde 2023, excepto en Japón, cuya tendencia creciente se ha pronunciado desde entonces.
El ascenso de las tasas de interés de largo plazo ha sido un fenómeno esencialmente de las economías avanzadas, si bien ha admitido excepciones, como Suiza, donde el aumento ha sido mínimo. En promedio, las economías emergentes han experimentado menores presiones, incluyendo reducciones en el caso de China e incrementos muy bajos en otras economías asiáticas. En el periodo de referencia, las tasas de interés de México a treinta y diez años aumentaron 150 y 160 puntos base, respectivamente.
A juzgar por la información extraíble de instrumentos de mercado, el aumento de las tasas de interés de largo plazo de las economías avanzadas no parece responder a un incremento en la inflación esperada. Las mediciones de compensación por inflación y riesgo inflacionario, definidas como la diferencia entre las tasas de interés nominales y reales, comúnmente conocidas como breakevens, han mostrado relativa estabilidad en el periodo de referencia.
Tampoco las presiones en las tasas de interés parecen reflejar un incremento material en el riesgo de impago de la deuda soberana. Por ejemplo, los precios de los contratos de seguro frente al impago de la deuda (CDS) se han mantenido estables o han aumentado ligeramente, reflejando un moderado riesgo crediticio. En otras palabras, los mercados financieros no revelan un temor de una crisis financiera y eventual default para estos países, por ejemplo, al estilo de la ocurrida en Grecia durante 2010-2012.
Una consecuencia del alza de las tasas de interés de largo plazo ha consistido en que los gobiernos han buscado emitir más deuda a corto plazo y menos a largo plazo. La menor duración de la deuda ha permitido disminuir el costo de financiamiento actual, pero ha aumentado las necesidades de refinanciación futuras.
Las mayores tasas de interés de largo plazo de las economías avanzadas parecen tener su raíz en las políticas fiscales expansivas de esos países, cuya agudización reciente ocurrió en 2020 para hacer frente a la pandemia, lo que se ha traducido en una demanda creciente de financiamiento en los mercados financieros.
Un caso emblemático ha sido Estados Unidos, cuya deuda federal en manos del público, como proporción del PIB, alcanzó 103 por ciento en el segundo trimestre de 2020, 25 puntos porcentuales por arriba de la correspondiente razón dos trimestres antes. Después de una moderada disminución, este indicador volvió a subir hasta alcanzar 99 por ciento en el primer trimestre de 2026.
Las tendencias alcistas de las tasas de interés estadounidenses podrían llegar a poner presión a la Reserva Federal para volver a aplicar programas masivos de compra de activos financieros (QE) con el fin de comprimir los rendimientos. Tal esfuerzo podría confundir la misión del banco central con la política fiscal, poniendo en peligro el control de la inflación.

Durante el mismo periodo, los rendimientos de los bonos de diez años de esos países registraron aumentos similares a los de treinta años, alcanzando niveles elevados desde 2023, excepto en Japón, cuya tendencia creciente se ha pronunciado desde entonces.

Durante el mismo periodo, los rendimientos de los bonos de diez años de esos países registraron aumentos similares a los de treinta años, alcanzando niveles elevados desde 2023, excepto en Japón, cuya tendencia creciente se ha pronunciado desde entonces.

Durante el mismo periodo, los rendimientos de los bonos de diez años de esos países registraron aumentos similares a los de treinta años, alcanzando niveles elevados desde 2023, excepto en Japón, cuya tendencia creciente se ha pronunciado desde entonces.

Desde finales de 2021, las tasas de interés de largo plazo de los bonos gubernamentales de la mayoría de las economías avanzadas han mostrado trayectorias ascendentes hasta alcanzar, en algunos casos, niveles no observados desde antes de la gran crisis financiera global de 2007-2008.

Durante el mismo periodo, los rendimientos de los bonos de diez años de esos países registraron aumentos similares a los de treinta años, alcanzando niveles elevados desde 2023, excepto en Japón, cuya tendencia creciente se ha pronunciado desde entonces.

Un caso emblemático ha sido Estados Unidos, cuya deuda federal en manos del público, como proporción del PIB, alcanzó 103 por ciento en el segundo trimestre de 2020, 25 puntos porcentuales por arriba de la correspondiente razón dos trimestres antes. Después de una moderada disminución, este indicador volvió a subir hasta alcanzar 99 por ciento en el primer trimestre de 2026.

Tal esfuerzo podría confundir la misión del banco central con la política fiscal, poniendo en peligro el control de la inflación.

deduped_items.title: Yategate: el nuevo juez de la causa ordenó una batería de medidas sobre los bienes de Martín Insaurralde y Jesica Cirio
deduped_items.summary: En una resolución, Rodríguez Ponte solicitó datos a registros inmuebles, telefónicas, escribanos y contadores. También pidió peritar los nuevos videos en que se ve a la modelo contando miles de dólares en un vestidor que reveló Clarín.
deduped_items.body_text:
En una medida que muestra su compromiso con investigar, el nuevo juez federal de Lomas de Zamora Juan Tomas Rodríguez Ponte dispuso este miércoles más de veinte medidas de prueba para profundizar la causa por enriquecimiento ilícito y lavado de dinero contra el ex intendente de Lomas de Zamora Martín Insaurralde y su ex esposa Jesica Cirio.
En una resolución a la que accedió Clarin, Rodríguez Ponte –quien asumió después de la feria judicial de julio en ese juzgado- pidió más medidas patrimoniales y sobre las comunicaciones de los imputados en la causa del yategate.
También pidió peritar los nuevos videos en que se ve a la modelo contando miles de dólares en un vestidor. Y dispuso seguir investigando a la modelo Sofía Clérici.

deduped_items.title: Why the US Dollar Won’t Fix the Venezuelan Economy
deduped_items.summary: Full dollarization fails to address the root causes of mismanagement and risks crippling long-term capacities
deduped_items.body_text:
Why the US Dollar Won’t Fix the Venezuelan Economy
Full dollarization fails to address the root causes of mismanagement and risks crippling long-term capacities
A few weeks ago, non-chavista politician Antonio Ecarri and American economist Steve Hanke managed to unearth one of Venezuela’s longstanding and unsettling debates: whether the country’s economy should be formally dollarized. After decades of economic hardship brought by repeated devaluations, hyperinflation and scarcity, the country’s monetary regime is heavily fragmented.
De facto dollarization rules most of the transactions, while the bolívar, crypto stablecoins, euros and the currencies of neighboring countries split the rest of the monetary market share used to maneuver through Venezuela’s complex economy. With the US pushing for the country’s economic stabilization to increase trust in foreign investors, the fragmented monetary ecosystem can be detrimental to the process made so far.
Venezuela’s economic outlook has improved after Maduro’s capture and since the US took control over Delcy’s decisions. Mainly because of a sharp recovery of oil exports to the US; by April, these were up 192% from their 2025 average. The energy sector is spearheading the recovery while attempting to partially compensate for the devastation caused by the twin earthquakes. GDP growth projections for Venezuela are forecasted at 5.8%, almost four times the country’s 2025 growth (1.5%). Yet the threat of inflation and instability compounds investors’ worries about entering the country. After repeated announcements by the interim regime promising to close the exchange gap and tackle inflation, their actions show otherwise.
Delcy continues to erode the bolívar by stimulating the money printer needed to feed chavismo’s patronage system. Exchange rate controls, which have long incentivized corruption and inflation, are still there. On the dollar side, credit loans and transactions remain “officially” forbidden, creating an artificial tax on USD transactions and fear amongst businesses who can be punished for their use.
Eliminating inflation would require abolishing all existing exchange rates and creating a new one based on an agreed technocratic approach.
The result of this unaddressed monetary disaster has been a persistent rise in inflation, which increased by 6.1% in July, bringing year-on-year inflation to 576% and 2026 cumulative inflation to 175.5%.
This is not the first time the call for dollarization has been in the spotlight in Venezuela. Nonetheless, US control over the country’s economy may increase the possibility of it becoming a reality. While dollarizing might be an effective measure to rapidly generate trust and reduce inflation, it raises important questions about its implementation under the interim regime and the future of Venezuela’s monetary sovereignty. Similar to Trump’s oil deal or the post-earthquake reconstruction, all discussions and actions are taking place behind the scenes, sidelining the very population that will have to deal with its consequences.
The US dollar is not the solution
Discussions regarding dollarization have primarily focused on three benefits: eliminating inflation, forcing fiscal discipline, and eradicating corruption. However, as long as those managing the dollarization process are the same ones who have guided Venezuela to the worst economic crisis in the region’s history, the result might be equally as bad but with a different set of consequences.
Hanke asserts that no preexisting institutional, fiscal or political conditions are necessary for dollarization to be successful. However, this process requires the willingness of all three areas to move forward. Eliminating inflation would require abolishing all existing exchange rates and creating a new one based on an agreed technocratic approach. Currently, there is no incentive for anyone in the interim regime’s leadership to converge the exchange rates.
A struggling or failed dollarization pl

deduped_items.title: More champagne for a few, no water for All: SA’s water tanker disaster
deduped_items.summary: South Africa’s water crisis is no longer just about dry taps, but what happens when emergency measures become a permanent business model. As municipalities spend hundreds of millions on water tankers, people remain trapped without reliable infrastructure. The question is no longer whether tankers are necessary, but who benefits when the emergency never ends and how long South Africans can afford to pay for failure.

deduped_items.title: France tries 14 over deadliest Channel migrant crossing disaster
deduped_items.summary: Fourteen people are to go on trial in France on Tuesday over the loss of 31 people including a seven-year-old child in 2021, in the deadliest small-boat crossing accident recorded in the Channel.
deduped_items.body_text:
Audio By Vocalize
Fourteen people are to go on trial in France on Tuesday over the loss of 31 people including a seven-year-old child in 2021, in the deadliest small-boat crossing accident recorded in the Channel.
The defendants, believed to be linked to people-smuggling networks, are accused of playing a role in the sinking in which 27 people, mainly Iraqi Kurds, were confirmed dead when their inflatable dinghy sank in the early hours of November 24, 2021.
Four others are still unaccounted for. Only two men survived the tragedy.
On November 24, 2021, a French fishing vessel reported several lifeless bodies floating in the Channel off Calais, close to British waters.
According to testimony from the two survivors, their flimsy boat began to deflate and take on water after several hours at sea.
Passengers fell overboard and drowned one after another, despite making around a dozen desperate calls for help to French and British rescue services.
The victims, aged between 7 and 46, were mostly Iraqi Kurds, but also included Afghans, Ethiopians and Egyptians.
Thousands of migrants each year seek to reach Britain from France in search of a better life.
The trial carries particular significance because of the high death toll and the sheer number of civil parties involved, 114 in all, including victims' families and around a dozen relatives who travelled from Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region.
The 14 individuals, most of them born in Afghanistan, face charges including manslaughter and facilitating illegal immigration as part of an organised criminal group.
Two of them, including an Afghan man, are the subject of arrest warrants and will be tried in absentia.
The case is also high-profile because of another highly sensitive strand of the investigation, which is still ongoing.
Seven French military personnel, five members at a maritime rescue coordination centre and two sailors aboard a patrol vessel have been under investigation since 2023 for failing to help a person in danger.
A UK inquiry released in February found some of the deaths would have been "avoidable" if British and French authorities had acted sooner to rescue those onboard.
Stay informed. Subscribe to our newsletter
Despite several distress calls, it was nearly 12 hours after the first pleas for help before the boat was finally found by a French fishing vessel.
By that time, most of those on board had drowned.
The separate case could eventually lead to another trial.
"Justice must hold accountable everyone who played a role in this tragedy," said lawyer Matthieu Chirez, who represents 113 civil parties.
Another lawyer, Emmanuel Daoud, expressed hope that the three-week trial would be an opportunity to see would-be migrants not as "statistics or commodities, but human beings in search of a better life."
Prosecutors have accused the defendants of helping launch a "substandard small boat, uncertified, unfit for navigation on the open sea, overcrowded and lacking appropriate life jackets."
Liability has also been extended to those accused of transporting, housing or accompanying the victims, actions that formed part of a "chain of successive events" leading to the tragedy, according to investigators.
The defendants have denied being smugglers and disputed their responsibility, or have presented themselves as migrants seeking to make the journey themselves.
However, phone records and location tracking placed several of them near the departure site and linked them to organising crossings to Britain.
The investigation uncovered two migrant-smuggling networks, one Afghan and the other Iraqi.

Fourteen people are to go on trial in France on Tuesday over the loss of 31 people including a seven-year-old child in 2021, in the deadliest small-boat crossing accident recorded in the Channel.
The defendants, believed to be linked to people-smuggling networks, are accused of playing a role in the sinking in which 27 people, mainly Iraqi Kurds, were confirmed dead when their inflatable dinghy sank in the early hours of November 24, 2021.
Four others are still unaccounted for. Only two men survived the tragedy.
On November 24, 2021, a French fishing vessel reported several lifeless bodies floating in the Channel off Calais, close to British waters.
According to testimony from the two survivors, their flimsy boat began to deflate and take on water after several hours at sea.
Passengers fell overboard and drowned one after another, despite making around a dozen desperate calls for help to French and British rescue services.
The victims, aged between 7 and 46, were mostly Iraqi Kurds, but also included Afghans, Ethiopians and Egyptians.
Thousands of migrants each year seek to reach Britain from France in search of a better life.
The trial carries particular significance because of the high death toll and the sheer number of civil parties involved, 114 in all, including victims' families and around a dozen relatives who travelled from Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region.
The 14 individuals, most of them born in Afghanistan, face charges including manslaughter and facilitating illegal immigration as part of an organised criminal group.
Two of them, including an Afghan man, are the subject of arrest warrants and will be tried in absentia.
The case is also high-profile because of another highly sensitive strand of the investigation, which is still ongoing.
Seven French military personnel, five members at a maritime rescue coordination centre and two sailors aboard a patrol vessel have been under investigation since 2023 for failing to help a person in danger.
A UK inquiry released in February found some of the deaths would have been "avoidable" if British and French authorities had acted sooner to rescue those onboard.
Stay informed. Subscribe to our newsletter
Despite several distress calls, it was nearly 12 hours after the first pleas for help before the boat was finally found by a French fishing vessel.
By that time, most of those on board had drowned.
The separate case could eventually lead to another trial.
"Justice must hold accountable everyone who played a role in this tragedy," said lawyer Matthieu Chirez, who represents 113 civil parties.
Another lawyer, Emmanuel Daoud, expressed hope that the three-week trial would be an opportunity to see would-be migrants not as "statistics or commodities, but human beings in search of a better life."
Prosecutors have accused the defendants of helping launch a "substandard small boat, uncertified, unfit for navigation on the open sea, overcrowded and lacking appropriate life jackets."
Liability has also been extended to those accused of transporting, housing or accompanying the victims, actions that formed part of a "chain of successive events" leading to the tragedy, according to investigators.
The defendants have denied being smugglers and disputed their responsibility, or have presented themselves as migrants seeking to make the journey themselves.
However, phone records and location tracking placed several of them near the departure site and linked them to organising crossings to Britain.
The investigation uncovered two migrant-smuggling networks, one Afghan and the other Iraqi.

On November 24, 2021, a French fishing vessel reported several lifeless bodies floating in the Channel off Calais, close to British waters.
According to testimony from the two survivors, their flimsy boat began to deflate and take on water after several hours at sea.
Passengers fell overboard and drowned one after another, despite making around a dozen desperate calls for help to French and British rescue services.

deduped_items.title: Ghana: Supreme Court Controversy - Bishops Call for Greater Caution, Not Resignation
deduped_items.summary: [Agenzia Fides] Accra -- The Chief Justice of Ghana, Paul Baffoe-Bonnie, should exercise greater caution when making public statements, but there are no grounds to call for his resignation. This, in essence, is the position of the Ghana Catholic Bishops' Conference regarding the controversy sparked by remarks made by Baffoe-Bonnie on September 2, 2026, during working visits to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) and the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF).

This, in essence, is the position of the Ghana Catholic Bishops' Conference regarding the controversy sparked by remarks made by Baffoe-Bonnie on September 2, 2026, during working visits to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) and the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF).

deduped_items.title: Transition énergétique: la facture de l'après-pétrole sera lourde pour les pétro-États
deduped_items.summary: La sortie mondiale du pétrole pourrait entraîner des conflits, des migrations et des bouleversements économiques selon une étude du groupe de réflexion E3G publiée mardi 8 septembre. L’utilisation du pétrole est en déclin dans de nombreux pays, avec la croissance des énergies renouvelables, et les effets de la guerre en Iran qui a limité l’offre et fait flamber les prix. Et cette stagnation va obliger les producteurs à rechercher un bassin d’acheteurs en déclin. Des pays comme le Nigeria, l’Iran

deduped_items.title: Elyanna faces backlash over prison visuals in ‘BOSA’ music video
deduped_items.summary: Elyanna faces backlash over prison visuals in ‘BOSA’ music video Submitted by Ayah El-Khaldi on Tue, 09/08/2026 - 14:17 Viewers question Palestinian-Chilean singer's decision to use jail as backdrop amid grim reality of Palestinian women in Israeli detention Elyanna features in a scene from her “BOSA” music video, which has drawn criticism over its use of prison imagery (Screenshot/YouTube) Off Palestinian singer Elyanna has drawn criticism over her latest music video, with viewers questioning t
deduped_items.body_text:
Elyanna faces backlash over prison visuals in ‘BOSA’ music video
Palestinian singer Elyanna has drawn criticism over her latest music video, with viewers questioning the decision to set the lively and playful clip in a jail while Palestinian women face widespread abuse in Israeli prisons.
Released on 4 September, BOSA opens with Elyanna behind metal bars. The video then moves through a stone prison-like compound, where she and a group of female dancers perform in courtyards and around barred windows. Throughout the song Elyanna is inviting the listener to “give [her] a kiss, kiss".
The women eventually walk out of the compound. Speaking to Complex MENA, Elyanna said: “With BOSA, I invite women to be loud about their femininity, desire, confidence, and freedom.”
But for some viewers, the prison setting was difficult to separate from the reality of Palestinians in Israeli detention.
“Wtf why is this set in a prison?” one commenter wrote under a promotional clip of the video.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Another asked whether “no one on the team” had considered that the concept might be “distasteful”.
Some also critcised the dancing and accused Elyanna of “self-orientalism”, arguing that Palestinian, Arab and South Asian motifs and dancing were purposefully transformed into “exotic” visual aesthetics that cater to the western gaze.
Can someone help explain to the “it’s just a music video crowd” that prison is not an abstract symbol for Palestinians. The prison is an actual institution of colonial violence. Palestinian prisoners have been subjected to torture, sexual abuse, humiliation and other forms of… https://t.co/N3UMmYZekA
— Nerdeen Kiswani (@NerdeenKiswani) September 7, 2026
“Honestly as a Palestinian. this isn’t it,” another viewer wrote.
The reaction has also played out on X, where users have questioned the decision to turn a jail into the backdrop for a stylised music video.
Edward Said rolling in his grave lmfao https://t.co/l3Fz4f9Q8F
— Charbel (@7elo3anepls) September 5, 2026
“This so beyond tone deaf *especially* in this climate,” posted one user. “Our women are burying their kids, getting kidnapped, jailed and sexually abused by the iof [Israeli Occupation Forces, Israeli army] every single day. and "عطيني بوسة" [give me a kiss] at the men who locked her up… the orientalist gaze… yeah this is NOT it.”
The response comes as Palestinian women and girls continue to face abuse in Israeli prisons.
Harsh prison conditions
Nearly 100 female Palestinian prisoners are currently held in Israeli detention, according to Palestinian organisations, including pregnant women and teenage girls.
Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir boasts of worsening conditions for Palestinian prisoners during a visit to female inmates, after one prisoner tells him they lack basic necessities. pic.twitter.com/OC6WytNUxv
— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) August 30, 2026
Former detainees and rights groups have described conditions including inadequate food, restrictions on hygiene and medical care, strip searches and other forms of abuse.
And the issue was particularly visible in the days before BOSA was released.
Israel’s far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir filmed himself on 30 August at Damon Prison, where dozens of female Palestinian prisoners are held. 
After a prisoner complains about the harsh conditions, including a lack of proper showers, Ben Gvir says: “I am pleased with these conditions.”
On social media, he described the issues raised by the Palestinian woman as “whining”, saying the days of “summer camp” in Israeli prisons were over, and boasted that he was responsible for reducing conditions to what he called the “bare minimum”.
i cannot get over how awful this is. what are you, as a palestinian woman, doing singing "give me a kiss", while playing the role of a woman

deduped_items.body_text:
9/11 at 25: Trump finds new targets for America's endless war on terror
On 11 September 2001, I was driving to work on the freeway in Austin, Texas when I heard the news on the radio that planes had crashed into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon.
As I went about nearly crashing my own car while trying to phone my best friend in New York City, I remember thinking that we were going to be hearing a lot about this particular date for a long time to come.
Sure enough, a quarter of a century has now passed since 9/11, and the events of that day continue to shape daily existence in the US - as trite as it sounds to say it.
Those of us who are old enough may remember the pre-9/11 panorama, when it was still possible to go through airport security with your water bottle and shampoo and Muslims could go to mosque without being pursued by FBI informants.
And while the US was never exactly all it was cracked up to be in terms of democracy and respect for basic rights, 9/11 definitively obliterated the right to privacy and other civil liberties upon which the country was supposedly founded.

Obviously, the fallout of 9/11 was quite a bit more physically and psychologically catastrophic for many people beyond US borders - like the millions of humans from Afghanistan to Iraq and beyond who were killed, mutilated, irradiated and otherwise targeted by the so-called "global war on terror".
Recall, too, the CIA's ritual torture at assorted international "black sites" and a certain infamous illegal US penal colony on occupied Cuban territory.
Terrorism, defined
It has become almost tiresome to have to repeat, time and again, that this alleged war on terror has itself constituted terrorism plain and simple - at least if we go by, say, the Cambridge Dictionary definition of the word: "violent action or threats designed to cause fear among ordinary people, in order to achieve political aims".
It has become almost tiresome to have to repeat, time and again, that this alleged war on terror has itself constituted terrorism plain and simple
Indeed, it goes without saying that the US military's habit of indiscriminate slaughter has done much to instil fear among ordinary people. Drone strikes on wedding parties are but one example of, um, "violent action".
As per the official narrative, of course, the US is always and forever a victim of terrorism rather than its preeminent perpetrator - a line that is perennially propagated by a disgraceful corporate media establishment that declines under any circumstances to speak truth to power.
To be sure, the US has gotten a run for its money on the whole terror-victimhood front from Israel, which refuses to cede its self-appointed position as number one victim of terrorism in the history of the world - and never mind its lengthy history of terrorising Palestinians.
Predictably, Israel wasted no time in jumping on the post-9/11 "war on terror" bandwagon, paving the way for eventual all-out genocide in the Gaza Strip, which now proceeds apace with US backing and in spite of an ostensible ceasefire.
Scared silly
It bears mentioning that, in addition to sowing terror across the globe, the US government has done a bang-up job in causing fear among its own citizens to further political goals.
In the immediate aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, ordinary people in the US were liable to believe that, if we didn't start blowing up other countries willy-nilly, we'd all be annihilated by anthrax-dispersing crop dusters or worse.
Granted, George W Bush - on whose presidential watch 9/11 took place and who was thus in charge of leading the country to war - was not the most fear-inspiring warrior, perhaps due in part to his pathological inability to formulate proper sentences.

deduped_items.title: Cameroon: Six skulls, a century in exile and a colonial history still to be unearthed
deduped_items.summary: After a rare and elaborate ceremony, six skulls belonging to Cameroonian chiefs were repatriated from Germany in July. With around 600 sets of human remains still in the European country, how will the vast human and cultural heritage plundered by colonial powers be returned?
deduped_items.body_text:
On 16 July 2026, an unusual ceremony took place at the University of Freiburg in Germany: six skulls, kept in jars for more than a century, were brought out of the laboratory. Some, their jawbones detached, arrived in several pieces. They were placed in coffins, following a ritual set out by a delegation – including traditional chiefs, academics and senior officials – that had travelled from Cameroon for the occasion.

deduped_items.title: صفعتان في يوم واحد: هل يبدأ حصار نتنياهو بعد التصعيد الأوروبي؟
deduped_items.summary: في قراءة الصحف اليوم: زلزال سياسي في إسرائيل بعد الكشف عن تحذير إماراتي مباشر لنتنياهو قبل هجوم السابع من أكتوبر، فيما تواجه حكومته ضربة دبلوماسية جديدة بعد قرار اثنتي عشرة دولة، بينها فرنسا وبريطانيا وكندا، حظر التجارة مع المستوطنات الإسرائيلية غير القانونية. الصحف البريطانية منقسمة بين من يرى في الخطوة دفاعاً عن حل الدولتين ومن يعتبرها إجراءً رمزياً قد يأتي بنتائج عكسية. وفي فرنسا، نتائج صادمة لتصنيف «بيزا» تفتح نقاشاً واسعاً حول تراجع مستوى التلاميذ، بين من يحمّل الشاشات وشبكات التواصل المسؤو

deduped_items.summary: في قراءة الصحف اليوم: زلزال سياسي في إسرائيل بعد الكشف عن تحذير إماراتي مباشر لنتنياهو قبل هجوم السابع من أكتوبر، فيما تواجه حكومته ضربة دبلوماسية جديدة بعد قرار اثنتي عشرة دولة، بينها فرنسا وبريطانيا وكندا، حظر التجارة مع المستوطنات الإسرائيلية غير القانونية. الصحف البريطانية منقسمة بين من يرى في الخطوة دفاعاً عن حل الدولتين ومن يعتبرها إجراءً رمزياً قد يأتي بنتائج عكسية. وفي فرنسا، نتائج صادمة لتصنيف «بيزا» تفتح نقاشاً واسعاً حول تراجع مستوى التلاميذ، بين من يحمّل الشاشات وشبكات التواصل المسؤو

deduped_items.title: Investigación de 'Haaretz' revela que EAU advirtió a Netanyahu del ataque del 7-O
deduped_items.summary: El periódico 'Haaretz' aseguró que una semana y media antes del ataque de Hamás del 7 de octubre de 2023 contra el sur de Israel, el presidente de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, el jeque Mohamed bin Zayed, advirtió por teléfono al primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, de que Hamás preparaba una operación que describía como "un terremoto" y que Netanyahu había asegurado al mandatario emiratí que su país estaba preparado para "cualquier escenario". El premier niega haber mantenido esa conversa

deduped_items.title: Colombia flexibiliza el porte de armas: ¿cuál es el riesgo de la medida?
deduped_items.summary: Este 8 de septiembre, el presidente de Colombia, Abelardo de la Espriella, levantó el decreto que suspendía los permisos para el porte de armas de fuego, una propuesta que prometió en campaña. De la Espriella argumentó que abre la posibilidad a los "ciudadanos de bien" de que "se puedan defender". La medida ha despertado las críticas de un sector de la población y ya ha sido aplicada en otros países de la región. Analizamos el tema con Ariel Ávila, senador de Colombia por el partido Alianza Verd
deduped_items.normalised_title: colombia flexibiliza el porte de armas cuál es el riesgo de la medida

deduped_items.title: EE. UU. y Colombia firman acuerdos para "reconstruir" el país y fortalecer su relación
deduped_items.summary: El presidente de Colombia, Abelardo de la Espriella, y el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, se reunieron en Barranquilla, donde sus delegaciones firmaron dos memorandos de entendimiento para "reconstruir" y fortalecer la relación bilateral. El primer acuerdo busca garantizar las cadenas de suministro de minerales y el segundo aborda la cooperación en energía nuclear de uso civil. Estos memorandos también forman parte de la estrategia colombiana para lograr la suspensión tempor

deduped_items.title: Synod: Reports published on relations between bishops, consecrated life, and ad limina visits
deduped_items.summary: The General Secretariat of the Synod on Tuesday released the Final Report of Study Group No. 6 on the review, from a synodal and missionary perspective, of the documents on relations between bishops, consecrated life, and ecclesial associations. It also released the second part – concerning ad limina visits – of the Final Report of Study Group No. 7 on certain aspects of the figure and ministry of the bishop from a synodal and missionary perspective. deduped_items.title: As 9/11 anniversary falls on Rosh Hashanah, Jews are asked to remember — and move forward
deduped_items.summary: NEW YORK (RNS) — As the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks coincides with the Jewish new year, Jewish leaders, rabbis and their interfaith partners reflect on what it means to remember — and how to live with what cannot be forgotten.
